1: // Sleep cycle (AGENTS.md section 8). Preview-first: preview() computes the
2: // full action plan and mutates nothing; execute() takes a backup snapshot
3: // first and exposes restore(). Guardrails: superseding/current records,
4: // derived/synthesized memories, and relationship hubs are NEVER archived.
5: 
6: import { DAY_MS, DEFAULTS } from "./types.ts";
7: import type { MemoryRecord, SleepPreview, SleepReport } from "./types.ts";
8: import { cosine } from "./embeddings.ts";
9: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
10: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
11: 
12: const HUB_THRESHOLD = 3;
13: 
14: export class SleepCycleService {
15:   private backups = new Map<string, { records: MemoryRecord[]; seq: number }>();
16:   private backupSeq = 0;
17: 
18:   constructor(
19:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
20:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
21:     private clock: () => number,
22:     private actor: string
23:   ) {}
24: 
25:   preview(): SleepPreview {
26:     const now = this.clock();
27:     const all = this.store.all();
28:     const referenced = new Set<string>();
29:     for (const m of all) {
30:       for (const r of m.relatedTo) referenced.add(r);
31:       if (m.supersedes) referenced.add(m.supersedes);
32:       for (const d of m.derivedFrom ?? []) referenced.add(d);
33:     }
34: 
35:     const toConsolidate = all
36:       .filter((m) => m.layer === "short_term" && now - m.lastAccessed >= DEFAULTS.consolidationDays * DAY_MS)
37:       .map((m) => m.id);
38: 
39:     const toArchive = all
40:       .filter((m) => {
41:         const oldEnough = now - m.timestamp >= DEFAULTS.archiveMinDays * DAY_MS;
42:         const lowAccess = m.accessCount <= DEFAULTS.archiveMaxAccess;
43:         const unreferenced = !referenced.has(m.id);
44:         if (!(oldEnough && lowAccess && unreferenced)) return false;
45:         // Guardrails (section 8.2): never archive these three classes.
46:         if (m.supersedes) return false;                       // superseding/current record
47:         if ((m.derivedFrom ?? []).length > 0) return false;   // derived/synthesized memory
48:         if (m.relatedTo.length >= HUB_THRESHOLD) return false; // relationship hub
49:         return true;
50:       })
51:       .map((m) => m.id);
52: 
53:     const toSynthesize: string[][] = [];
54:     const used = new Set<string>();
55:     for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
56:       if (used.has(all[i].id)) continue;
57:       const group = [all[i]];
58:       for (let j = i + 1; j < all.length; j++) {
59:         if (used.has(all[j].id)) continue;
60:         if (cosine(all[i].embedding, all[j].embedding) >= DEFAULTS.synthesisCosine) group.push(all[j]);
61:       }
62:       if (group.length >= 2) {
63:         for (const g of group) used.add(g.id);
64:         toSynthesize.push(group.map((g) => g.id));
65:       }
66:     }
67: 
68:     return { toConsolidate, toArchive, toSynthesize };
69:   }
70: 
71:   execute(preview?: SleepPreview): SleepReport {
72:     const plan = preview ?? this.preview();
73:     const backupId = `backup-${++this.backupSeq}`;
74:     this.backups.set(backupId, this.store.snapshotAll());
75:     const actionLog: string[] = [`backup ${backupId} created`];
76: 
77:     for (const id of plan.toConsolidate) {
78:       const m = this.store.get(id);
79:       if (!m) continue;
80:       this.store.promote(id, "long_term");
81:       this.ledger.log(id, "sleep_consolidate", this.actor, { details: { from: "short_term", to: "long_term" } });
82:       actionLog.push(`consolidated ${id}`);
83:     }
84: 
85:     for (const id of plan.toArchive) {
86:       const m = this.store.get(id);
87:       if (!m) continue;
88:       this.ledger.log(id, "sleep_archive", this.actor, { details: { age: this.clock() - m.timestamp, accessCount: m.accessCount } });
89:       this.store.delete(id, "sleep archive");
90:       actionLog.push(`archived ${id}`);
91:     }
92: 
93:     let synthesized = 0;
94:     for (const group of plan.toSynthesize) {
95:       const members = group.map((id) => this.store.get(id)).filter((m): m is MemoryRecord => !!m);
96:       if (members.length < 2) continue;
97:       const merged = this.store.add({
98:         content: `Synthesis: ${members.map((m) => m.content).join(" | ")}`,
99:         type: "factual",
100:         layer: "long_term",
101:         tags: [...new Set(members.flatMap((m) => m.tags))],
102:         confidence: Math.max(...members.map((m) => m.confidence)),
103:         source: "sleep:synthesis",
104:         provenance: { origin: "sleep_synthesis", learnedAt: this.clock(), label: `synthesized from ${members.length} memories` },
105:         derivedFrom: members.map((m) => m.id),
106:       });
107:       this.ledger.log(merged.id, "sleep_synthesize", this.actor, { details: { sources: group } });
108:       for (const m of members) this.store.delete(m.id, "merged by sleep synthesis");
109:       synthesized++;
110:       actionLog.push(`synthesized ${merged.id} from ${group.join(", ")}`);
111:     }
112: 
113:     this.store.persist();
114:     return {
115:       backupId,
116:       consolidated: plan.toConsolidate.length,
117:       archived: plan.toArchive.length,
118:       synthesized,
119:       actionLog,
120:     };
121:   }
122: 
123:   restore(backupId: string): void {
124:     const backup = this.backups.get(backupId);
125:     if (!backup) throw new Error(`H-MEM: unknown backup ${backupId}`);
126:     this.store.restoreAll(backup.records, backup.seq);
127:     this.ledger.log("*", "restore", this.actor, { details: { backupId } });
128:   }
129: }

1: // Dreaming (AGENTS.md section 7): constructive synthesis with a human
2: // approval boundary. Proposals are NEVER auto-materialized; only approve()
3: // turns one into durable memory, with derivedFrom lineage.
4: 
5: import { DEFAULTS } from "./types.ts";
6: import type { DreamProposal, MemoryRecord } from "./types.ts";
7: import { cosine, jaccard } from "./embeddings.ts";
8: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
9: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
10: 
11: export class DreamingService {
12:   private proposals = new Map<string, DreamProposal>();
13:   private seq = 0;
14: 
15:   constructor(
16:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
17:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
18:     private clock: () => number,
19:     private actor: string
20:   ) {}
21: 
22:   // Multi-signal relatedness: content similarity, tag overlap, shared domain/type, entity overlap.
23:   private relatedness(a: MemoryRecord, b: MemoryRecord): number {
24:     return (
25:       0.5 * Math.max(0, cosine(a.embedding, b.embedding)) +
26:       0.2 * jaccard(a.tags, b.tags) +
27:       0.1 * (a.domain === b.domain ? 1 : 0) +
28:       0.2 * jaccard(a.entities, b.entities)
29:     );
30:   }
31: 
32:   private cluster(): MemoryRecord[][] {
33:     const all = this.store.all();
34:     const used = new Set<string>();
35:     const clusters: MemoryRecord[][] = [];
36:     for (const seed of all) {
37:       if (used.has(seed.id)) continue;
38:       const group = [seed];
39:       for (const other of all) {
40:         if (other.id === seed.id || used.has(other.id)) continue;
41:         if (this.relatedness(seed, other) >= DEFAULTS.dreamRelatedness) group.push(other);
42:       }
43:       if (group.length >= DEFAULTS.dreamClusterMinSize) {
44:         for (const g of group) used.add(g.id);
45:         clusters.push(group);
46:       }
47:     }
48:     return clusters;
49:   }
50: 
51:   dream(): DreamProposal[] {
52:     const created: DreamProposal[] = [];
53:     const propose = (p: Omit<DreamProposal, "id" | "status">): void => {
54:       const proposal: DreamProposal = { ...p, id: `dream-${++this.seq}`, status: "proposed" };
55:       this.proposals.set(proposal.id, proposal);
56:       created.push(proposal);
57:       this.ledger.log(proposal.id, "dream_proposed", this.actor, { details: { type: p.type, derivedFrom: p.derivedFrom } });
58:     };
59: 
60:     // Insights from clusters.
61:     let insights = 0;
62:     for (const cluster of this.cluster()) {
63:       if (insights >= DEFAULTS.maxDreamProposalsPerType) break;
64:       const domains = [...new Set(cluster.map((m) => m.domain))].join("/");
65:       propose({
66:         type: "insight",
67:         content: `Across ${cluster.length} related memories (${domains}): ${cluster.map((m) => m.content).join(" + ")}`,
68:         derivedFrom: cluster.map((m) => m.id),
69:       });
70:       insights++;
71:     }
72: 
73:     // Domain suggestions for uncategorized memories.
74:     let domains = 0;
75:     for (const m of this.store.all()) {
76:       if (domains >= DEFAULTS.maxDreamProposalsPerType) break;
77:       if (m.domain !== "general") continue;
78:       const suggested = this.store.classifyDomain(m.content, m.tags, m.type);
79:       if (suggested !== "general") {
80:         propose({ type: "domain", content: `Reclassify "${m.content.slice(0, 60)}" as ${suggested}`, derivedFrom: [m.id], suggestedDomain: suggested });
81:         domains++;
82:       }
83:     }
84:

41:   const fresh: { obs: IngestObservation; checksum: string }[] = [];
42:   const skipped: IngestObservation[] = [];
43:   time(2, "cluster-classify", () => {

48:       else fresh.push({ obs, checksum });

50:   });

52:   // 3. Persist primary aggregates: upsert observation entities + mentioned entities.
53:   const records: ObservationRecord[] = [];

75:     const used = new Set<string>();

79:       used.add(seed.externalId);
80:       for (const other of all) {
81:         if (used.has(other.externalId)) continue;
82:         if (jaccard(seed.entityIds ?? [], other.entityIds ?? []) >= CLUSTER_JACCARD) {

96:   time(4, "score-measure", () => {

99:       const storyId = `story_${sha256Hex(canonicalJson(memberIds)).slice(0, 12)}`;

101:       const lastAt = times[times.length - 1];
102:       const velocity = (windowMs: number) => {
103:         // Bucketed rate: mentions inside the window ending at the newest
104:         // observation, divided by the window's hours. A naive
105:         // mentions/total-hours calculation fails trend detection.
106:         const inWindow = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - windowMs).length;
107:         return inWindow / (windowMs / HOUR_MS);

109:       const prevHour = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - 2 * HOUR_MS && t <= lastAt - HOUR_MS).length;
110:       const currHour = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - HOUR_MS).length;
111:       const score: ScoreSnapshot = {

113:         at: new Date(lastAt).toISOString(),

115:         velocity24h: velocity(24 * HOUR_MS),
116:         velocity7d: velocity(7 * 24 * HOUR_MS),
117:         trendDirection: Math.sign(currHour - prevHour) as -1 | 0 | 1,
118:       };

120:       store.scores.push(score);

122:       const entityIds = [...new Set(group.flatMap((g) => g.entityIds ?? []))].sort();
123:       const story: StoryAggregate = {

24: function rotr(x: number, n: number): number {
25:   return (x >>> n) | (x << (32 - n));
26: }

28: /** Hex-encoded sha-256 of a UTF-8 string. */
29: export function sha256Hex(input: string): string {
30:   const data = new TextEncoder().encode(input);
31:   const len = data.length;
32:   const bitLenHi = Math.floor((len / 0x20000000)) >>> 0;
33:   const bitLenLo = (len << 3) >>> 0;
34: 
35:   const paddedLen = (((len + 8) >> 6) + 1) << 6;
36:   const padded = new Uint8Array(paddedLen);
37:   padded.set(data);
38:   padded[len] = 0x80;
39:   const dv = new DataView(padded.buffer);
40:   dv.setUint32(paddedLen - 8, bitLenHi);
41:   dv.setUint32(paddedLen - 4, bitLenLo);
42: 
43:   let h0 = 0x6a09e667, h1 = 0xbb67ae85, h2 = 0x3c6ef372, h3 = 0xa54ff53a;
44:   let h4 = 0x510e527f, h5 = 0x9b05688c, h6 = 0x1f83d9ab, h7 = 0x5be0cd19;
45: 
46:   const w = new Uint32Array(64);
47:   for (let i = 0; i < paddedLen; i += 64) {
48:     for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) w[t] = dv.getUint32(i + t * 4);
49:     for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
50:       const s0 = rotr(w[t - 15], 7) ^ rotr(w[t - 15], 18) ^ (w[t - 15] >>> 3);
51:       const s1 = rotr(w[t - 2], 17) ^ rotr(w[t - 2], 19) ^ (w[t - 2] >>> 10);
52:       w[t] = (w[t - 16] + s0 + w[t - 7] + s1) >>> 0;
53:     }
54:     let a = h0, b = h1, c = h2, d = h3, e = h4, f = h5, g = h6, h = h7;
55:     for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
56:       const S1 = rotr(e, 6) ^ rotr(e, 11) ^ rotr(e, 25);
57:       const ch = (e & f) ^ (~e & g);
58:       const temp1 = (h + S1 + ch + K[t] + w[t]) >>> 0;
59:       const S0 = rotr(a, 2) ^ rotr(a, 13) ^ rotr(a, 22);
60:       const maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
61:       const temp2 = (S0 + maj) >>> 0;
62:       h = g; g = f; f = e;
63:       e = (d + temp1) >>> 0;
64:       d = c; c = b; b = a;
65:       a = (temp1 + temp2) >>> 0;
66:     }
67:     h0 = (h0 + a) >>> 0; h1 = (h1 + b) >>> 0; h2 = (h2 + c) >>> 0; h3 = (h3 + d) >>> 0;
68:     h4 = (h4 + e) >>> 0; h5 = (h5 + f) >>> 0; h6 = (h6 + g) >>> 0; h7 = (h7 + h) >>> 0;
69:   }
70: 
71:   return [h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]
72:     .map((x) => x.toString(16).padStart(8, "0"))
73:     .join("");
74: }

80: /**
81:  * Deterministic JSON serialization: object keys sorted, undefined members
82:  * dropped. JSON key order in JS is insertion order, so a naive
83:  * JSON.stringify comparison gives false negatives; the idempotency diff
84:  * (scripts/idempotency-check.ts) depends on this function instead.
85:  */
86: export function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string {
87:   if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") {
88:     const s = JSON.stringify(value);
89:     return s === undefined ? "null" : s;
90:   }
91:   if (Array.isArray(value)) {
92:     return "[" + value.map((v) => canonicalJson(v)).join(",") + "]";
93:   }
94:   const obj = value as Record<string, unknown>;
95:   const keys = Object.keys(obj)
96:     .filter((k) => obj[k] !== undefined)
97:     .sort();
98:   return "{" + keys.map((k) => JSON.stringify(k) + ":" + canonicalJson(obj[k])).join(",") + "}";
99: }

101: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
102: /* Name normalization                                                  */
103: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

105: /**
106:  * normalizeName per docs/stable-ids.md:
107:  *   NFKD normalize -> strip combining marks -> lowercase -> collapse whitespace -> trim
108:  *
109:  * Notes on the edge cases this must catch (dedupe correctness depends on it):
110:  * - Diacritics: "Jose Garcia" and the accented spelling must normalize identically
111:  *   (NFKD decomposes the accents into combining marks, which are then stripped).
112:  * - Non-breaking space (U+00A0): NFKD decomposes it to a regular space; the
113:  *   whitespace collapse then folds runs of any whitespace into one space.
114:  * - Zero-width characters (U+200B..U+200D, U+FEFF) carry no name content and are
115:  *   stripped explicitly, since NFKD leaves them alone.
116:  * - Over-normalization is the opposite failure: "Acme Corp" and
117:  *   "Acme Corporation" are DIFFERENT names and must produce DIFFERENT ids.
118:  *   Normalization never abbreviates, stems, or drops word characters.
119:  */
120: export function normalizeName(name: string): string {
121:   return name
122:     .normalize("NFKD")
123:     .replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, "") // strip combining marks
124:     .replace(/[​-‍﻿]/g, "") // strip zero-width chars
125:     .toLowerCase()
126:     .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
127:     .trim();
128: }

1: // Entity resolution (AGENTS.md section on merge detection). Banded thresholds:
2: //
3: //   similarity >= 0.85            -> auto-merge   (0.85 EXACTLY is auto-merge)
4: //   0.82 <= similarity < 0.85     -> operator review queue (0.82 EXACTLY queues)
5: //   similarity < 0.82             -> new entity
6: //
7: // Similarity is Levenshtein-based: 1 - distance / max(lenA, lenB), computed on
8: // NORMALIZED names (stableIds.normalizeName). The spec names the bands but not
9: // the normalization input; this reference pins it to normalized names so that
10: // diacritics and whitespace never inflate distance.
11: 
12: import { normalizeName } from "./stableIds.ts";
13: 
14: export function levenshtein(a: string, b: string): number {
15:   if (a === b) return 0;
16:   const m = a.length;
17:   const n = b.length;
18:   if (m === 0) return n;
19:   if (n === 0) return m;
20:   let prev = new Array<number>(n + 1);
21:   let curr = new Array<number>(n + 1);
22:   for (let j = 0; j <= n; j++) prev[j] = j;
23:   for (let i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
24:     curr[0] = i;
25:     for (let j = 1; j <= n; j++) {
26:       const cost = a[i - 1] === b[j - 1] ? 0 : 1;
27:       curr[j] = Math.min(prev[j] + 1, curr[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + cost);
28:     }
29:     [prev, curr] = [curr, prev];
30:   }
31:   return prev[n];
32: }
33: 
34: export function nameSimilarity(rawA: string, rawB: string): number {
35:   const a = normalizeName(rawA);
36:   const b = normalizeName(rawB);
37:   if (a.length === 0 && b.length === 0) return 1;
38:   const maxLen = Math.max(a.length, b.length);
39:   if (maxLen === 0) return 1;
40:   return 1 - levenshtein(a, b) / maxLen;
41: }
42: 
43: export type ResolutionDecision = "auto-merge" | "review" | "new";
44: 
45: export function decide(similarity: number, autoMergeAt = 0.85, reviewLower = 0.82): ResolutionDecision {
46:   if (similarity >= autoMergeAt) return "auto-merge"; // boundary value merges
47:   if (similarity >= reviewLower) return "review";     // boundary value queues
48:   return "new";
49: }
50: 
51: // Clustering gate for the ingest pipeline: entity-overlap Jaccard >= 0.5
52: // co-clusters two observations.
53: export function jaccard(a: Iterable<string>, b: Iterable<string>): number {
54:   const sa = new Set(a);
55:   const sb = new Set(b);
56:   if (sa.size === 0 || sb.size === 0) return 0;
57:   let inter = 0;
58:   for (const x of sa) if (sb.has(x)) inter++;
59:   return inter / (sa.size + sb.size - inter);
60: }

1: // Config manager (AGENTS.md section 4.1) plus the efficiency math from
2: // section 6 and docs/efficiency-model.md. Validation throws a typed error;
3: // nothing is silently truncated or ignored.
4: 
5: import {
6:   BOUNDS, ConfigValidationError, DEFAULT_CONFIG, FRAMING_TOKENS, OUTPUT_BUDGET,
7: } from "./types.ts";
8: import type { ChunkConfig, ChunkInfo } from "./types.ts";
9: 
10: export function resolveConfig(partial?: Partial<ChunkConfig>): ChunkConfig {
11:   const cfg: ChunkConfig = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...partial };
12:   for (const key of ["chunkSize", "maxChunks", "carryoverTokens", "overlapTokens"] as const) {
13:     const b = BOUNDS[key];
14:     const v = cfg[key];
15:     if (!Number.isFinite(v)) throw new ConfigValidationError(`${key} must be a number`);
16:     if (v < b.min || v > b.max) throw new ConfigValidationError(`${key}=${v} outside [${b.min}, ${b.max}]`);
17:     // Ruling: the spec's "step" values are UI slider granularity, not hard
18:     // validation. The spec's own default carryoverTokens=800 is unreachable
19:     // under a strict step-128 grid from min=128, so a strict reading would
20:     // reject the documented default. Only min/max are enforced here.
21:   }
22:   if (cfg.carryoverTokens <= 0) throw new ConfigValidationError("carryoverTokens must be > 0");
23:   if (cfg.chunkSize < FRAMING_TOKENS + cfg.carryoverTokens + OUTPUT_BUDGET) {
24:     throw new ConfigValidationError(
25:       `chunkSize=${cfg.chunkSize} < framing(${FRAMING_TOKENS}) + carryover(${cfg.carryoverTokens}) + outputBudget(${OUTPUT_BUDGET})`
26:     );
27:   }
28:   return cfg;
29: }
30: 
31: // Projected efficiency curve (section 4.1), 10 steps.
32: export function projectionCurve(cfg: ChunkConfig, steps = 10): { step: number; standard: number; markovian: number }[] {
33:   const out = [];
34:   for (let step = 1; step <= steps; step++) {
35:     const historySize = (step - 1) * cfg.chunkSize;
36:     out.push({
37:       step,
38:       standard: historySize + cfg.chunkSize,
39:       markovian: cfg.carryoverTokens + cfg.chunkSize,
40:     });
41:   }
42:   return out;
43: }
44: 
45: // Historical run efficiency (section 6.3). ALWAYS computed against the
46: // config passed in, which must be the run's own persisted snapshot.
47: export function runEfficiency(chunks: ChunkInfo[], cfg: ChunkConfig): {
48:   totalTokensUsed: number;
49:   standardCost: number;
50:   markovianCost: number;
51:   tokensSaved: number;
52:   efficiencyPercent: number;
53: } {
54:   const totalTokensUsed = chunks.reduce((s, c) => s + c.tokens, 0);
55:   let standardCost = 0;
56:   let prefix = 0;
57:   for (const c of chunks) {
58:     standardCost += prefix + c.tokens;
59:     prefix += c.tokens;
60:   }
61:   const markovianCost = chunks.length * cfg.carryoverTokens + totalTokensUsed;
62:   const tokensSaved = Math.max(0, standardCost - markovianCost);
63:   return {
64:     totalTokensUsed,
65:     standardCost,
66:     markovianCost,
67:     tokensSaved,
68:     efficiencyPercent: standardCost > 0 ? (tokensSaved / standardCost) * 100 : 0,
69:   };
70: }

83: export function modelTotals(N: number, k: CostModelConstants = DOC_DEFAULTS): {
84:   naiveTotal: number;
85:   markovianTotal: number;
86:   savings: number;
87:   efficiency: number; // 0..1

91:   //   markovian_total = N*(F + G + C + S)

93:   const markovianTotal = N * (k.F + k.G + k.C + k.S);
94:   const savings = naiveTotal - markovianTotal;
95:   return { naiveTotal, markovianTotal, savings, efficiency: savings / naiveTotal };

1: // Marker protocol (AGENTS.md section 3). Canonical markers are square-bracket:
2: // [STATE_CHECKPOINT] and [TASK_COMPLETE], with the listed backward-compatible
3: // variants. The angle-bracket forms (<CARRYOVER>, <DONE>, <PROGRESS>,
4: // <NEEDS_TOOL .../>) used across this engine's examples are accepted as
5: // additional detection aliases. Cleaning strips every form from display text.
6: 
7: export interface ParsedMarkers {
8:   state?: string;            // text captured after/inside a state marker
9:   done: boolean;             // final completion marker present
10:   progress?: string;         // optional progress note
11:   needsTool?: { tool: string; input: string };
12:   needsClarification?: string;
13:   cleaned: string;           // display-safe content, all markers stripped
14: }
15: 
16: const STATE_BLOCKS = [
17:   /<CARRYOVER>([\s\S]*?)<\/CARRYOVER>/g,
18: ];
19: const STATE_TAILS = [
20:   /\[STATE_CHECKPOINT\]\s*([\s\S]*)$/,
21:   /@@@STATE@@@\s*([\s\S]*)$/,
22:   /(?<!_)\[STATE\]\s*([\s\S]*)$/,
23:   /---STATE---\s*([\s\S]*)$/,
24: ];
25: const FINAL_MARKERS = [/\[TASK_COMPLETE\]/, /@@@FINAL@@@/, /(?<!_)\[FINAL\]/, /---FINAL---/, /<DONE\s*\/?>/];
26: const PROGRESS_BLOCK = /<PROGRESS>([\s\S]*?)<\/PROGRESS>/;
27: const NEEDS_TOOL = /[<[]NEEDS_TOOL\s+tool="([^"]+)"\s+input=(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')\s*\/?[\]>]/;
28: const NEEDS_CLARIFICATION = /[<[]NEEDS_CLARIFICATION[\]>]\s*([^\n]*)/;
29: 
30: export function parseMarkers(raw: string): ParsedMarkers {
31:   let state: string | undefined;
32:   let progress: string | undefined;
33:   let needsTool: ParsedMarkers["needsTool"];
34:   let needsClarification: string | undefined;
35: 
36:   for (const re of STATE_BLOCKS) {
37:     const matches = [...raw.matchAll(re)];
38:     if (matches.length) state = matches[matches.length - 1][1].trim();
39:   }
40:   if (state === undefined) {
41:     for (const re of STATE_TAILS) {
42:       const m = raw.match(re);
43:       if (m) {
44:         state = m[1].trim();
45:         break;
46:       }
47:     }
48:   }
49:   const done = FINAL_MARKERS.some((re) => re.test(raw));
50:   const p = raw.match(PROGRESS_BLOCK);
51:   if (p) progress = p[1].trim();
52:   const t = raw.match(NEEDS_TOOL);
53:   if (t) needsTool = { tool: t[1], input: t[2] ?? t[3] ?? "" };
54:   const c = raw.match(NEEDS_CLARIFICATION);
55:   if (c) needsClarification = c[1].trim();
56: 
57:   return { state, done, progress, needsTool, needsClarification, cleaned: cleanMarkers(raw) };
58: }
59: 
60: export function cleanMarkers(raw: string): string {
61:   let out = raw;
62:   out = out.replace(/<CARRYOVER>[\s\S]*?<\/CARRYOVER>/g, "");
63:   out = out.replace(/<PROGRESS>[\s\S]*?<\/PROGRESS>/g, "");
64:   out = out.replace(/[<[]NEEDS_TOOL[^\]>]*[\]>]/g, "");
65:   out = out.replace(/[<[]NEEDS_CLARIFICATION[\]>][^\n]*/g, "");
66:   out = out.replace(/\[STATE_CHECKPOINT\][\s\S]*$/, "");
67:   out = out.replace(/@@@STATE@@@[\s\S]*$/, "");
68:   out = out.replace(/---STATE---[\s\S]*$/, "");
69:   // bare [STATE] tail only when it starts a marker line, to avoid eating prose
70:   out = out.replace(/\n\[STATE\][\s\S]*$/, "");
71:   for (const re of [/\[TASK_COMPLETE\]/g, /@@@FINAL@@@/g, /---FINAL---/g, /<DONE\s*\/?>/g]) out = out.replace(re, "");
72:   out = out.replace(/\n\[FINAL\][\s\S]*$/, "");
73:   return out.replace(/[ \t]+$/gm, "").replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n").trim();
74: }

1: // State carryover service (AGENTS.md section 4.3). The compression cascade
2: // runs in strict order: marker override, LLM compression, heuristic
3: // extraction, tail truncation. Each level falls through on failure so the
4: // chain survives model/API instability.
5: 
6: import { estimateTokens } from "./types.ts";
7: import type { ChunkConfig } from "./types.ts";
8: 
9: export type CascadeLevel = "marker" | "llm" | "heuristic" | "truncation";
10: 
11: export interface CarryoverResult {
12:   carryover: string;
13:   level: CascadeLevel;
14: }
15: 
16: const KEY_PHRASE = /(?:^|\n|\.\s+)((?:Therefore|Key insight|Status|Decision|Decided|Next|Remaining|Completed)[^.\n]*)/gi;
17: 
18: export class CarryoverService {
19:   constructor(private compressorFn?: (prompt: string, systemPrompt: string) => Promise<string>) {}
20: 
21:   async next(args: {
22:     markerState: string | undefined;
23:     previousCarryover: string;
24:     chunkText: string;
25:     config: ChunkConfig;
26:   }): Promise<CarryoverResult> {
27:     const budget = args.config.carryoverTokens;
28: 
29:     // Level 1: explicit marker override. Accept iff >= 24 chars and within budget.
30:     if (args.markerState !== undefined) {
31:       const sanitized = args.markerState.replace(/[<>[\]@-]{3,}/g, "").trim();
32:       if (sanitized.length >= 24 && estimateTokens(sanitized) <= budget) {
33:         return { carryover: sanitized, level: "marker" };
34:       }
35:     }
36: 
37:     // Level 2: LLM-based compression via the injected compressor.
38:     if (this.compressorFn) {
39:       try {
40:         const preview = args.chunkText.slice(-2000);
41:         const prompt =
42:           `Previous state:\n${args.previousCarryover || "(none)"}\n\nLatest chunk (tail):\n${preview}\n\n` +
43:           `Compress into 3-5 critical points as a labeled block:\nCOMPLETED: ...\nREMAINING: ...\nDECISIONS: ...\nCONTEXT: ...`;
44:         const compressed = (await this.compressorFn(prompt, "You compress reasoning state. Be terse and lossless on decisions.")).trim();
45:         if (compressed.length >= 24 && estimateTokens(compressed) <= budget) {
46:           return { carryover: compressed, level: "llm" };
47:         }
48:       } catch {
49:         // fall through to heuristics
50:       }
51:     }
52: 
53:     // Level 3: heuristic key-phrase extraction.
54:     const phrases = [...args.chunkText.matchAll(KEY_PHRASE)].map((m) => m[1].trim()).slice(0, 5);
55:     if (phrases.length > 0) {
56:       const summary = phrases.join("; ");
57:       if (estimateTokens(summary) <= budget) return { carryover: summary, level: "heuristic" };

1: // Runtime orchestrator (AGENTS.md section 4.5). One function runs the whole
2: // chain: build prompt, invoke generator, clean markers, account tokens,
3: // compress state, persist chunk, detect completion. Reflection failure never
4: // fails the run (sections 7, 11). Abort is checked before each chunk and
5: // before compression.
6: 
7: import { cleanMarkers, parseMarkers } from "./markers.ts";
8: import { runEfficiency } from "./configManager.ts";
9: import { CarryoverService } from "./carryover.ts";
10: import { buildPrompt, overlapSlice } from "./promptBuilder.ts";
11: import { ProgressService } from "./progress.ts";
12: import { estimateTokens } from "./types.ts";
13: import type { Attachment, ChunkConfig, ChunkInfo, Generator, MarkovianRun, Mode, RunOptions, StepFn } from "./types.ts";
14: 
15: let runSeq = 0;
16: export function resetRunSeq(): void {
17:   runSeq = 0;
18: }
19: 
20: export async function orchestrate(args: {
21:   options: RunOptions;
22:   config: ChunkConfig;
23:   clock: () => number;
24:   progress: ProgressService;
25:   carryoverService: CarryoverService;
26:   defaultGenerator?: Generator;
27: }): Promise<MarkovianRun> {
28:   const { options, config, clock, progress, carryoverService } = args;
29:   const goal = options.goal ?? options.prompt;
30:   if (!goal) throw new Error("Markovian: run needs a goal or prompt");
31:   const mode: Mode = options.mode ?? "ARCHITECT";
32:   const attachments: Attachment[] = options.attachments ?? [];
33:   const generator = normalizeGenerator(options, args.defaultGenerator, goal);
34:   const start = clock();
35: 
36:   const run: MarkovianRun = {
37:     id: `run-${++runSeq}`,
38:     timestamp: start,
39:     prompt: goal.slice(0, 500),
40:     mode,
41:     chunkConfig: { ...config }, // mandatory per-run snapshot
42:     chunks: [],
43:     totalTokensUsed: 0,
44:     totalTokensSaved: 0,
45:     efficiencyPercent: 0,
46:     durationMs: 0,
47:     status: "completed",
48:     tokenLabel: "estimated",
49:     output: "",
50:   };
51: 
52:   const cleanedParts: string[] = [];
53:   let carryover = "";
54:   let previousCleaned = "";
55:   let accumulatedSavings = 0;
56:   let done = false;
57: 
58:   progress.phase("initializing", `${mode} chain, maxChunks=${config.maxChunks}`);
59: 
60:   try {
61:     while (run.chunks.length < config.maxChunks && !done) {
62:       if (options.abortSignal?.aborted) {
63:         run.status = "aborted";
64:         break;
65:       }
66:       const step = run.chunks.length + 1; // 1-based
67:       progress.phase("generating", `chunk ${step}`);
68: 
69:       const prompt = buildPrompt({
70:         mode,
71:         goal,
72:         step,
73:         carryover,
74:         overlapText: overlapSlice(previousCleaned, config),
75:         memoryContext: options.memoryContext,
76:         attachments: step === 1 ? attachments : [],
77:         config,
78:       });
79: 
80:       const { text } = await generator(prompt, step === 1 ? attachments : [], undefined, options.onStream, options.abortSignal);
81:       const parsed = parseMarkers(text);
82:       const content = parsed.cleaned;
83:       const chunkTokens = estimateTokens(content);
84: 
85:       // Section 6.1/6.2 savings accounting (estimated, chars/4).
86:       const historySize = (step - 1) * config.chunkSize;
87:       const standardChunkCost = historySize + chunkTokens;
88:       const markovianChunkCost = config.carryoverTokens + chunkTokens;
89:       accumulatedSavings += Math.max(0, standardChunkCost - markovianChunkCost);
90: 
91:       // Persist the generated chunk first: its cost is already paid, so an
92:       // abort after generation still preserves partial output (section 11).
93:       const chunk: ChunkInfo = { id: step, tokens: chunkTokens, carryover, content };
94:       run.chunks.push(chunk);
95:       cleanedParts.push(content);
96:       previousCleaned = content;
97:       progress.chunkDone(chunk);
98: 
99:       if (options.abortSignal?.aborted) {
100:         run.status = "aborted";
101:         break;
102:       }
103:       progress.phase("compressing", `chunk ${step}`);
104:       const next = await carryoverService.next({
105:         markerState: parsed.state,
106:         previousCarryover: carryover,
107:         chunkText: text,
108:         config,
109:       });
110:       carryover = next.carryover;
111:       progress.update({ tokensUsed: run.chunks.reduce((s, c) => s + c.tokens, 0), tokensSaved: accumulatedSavings, carryoverSize: estimateTokens(carryover) });
112: 
113:       if (parsed.done) done = true;
114:       if (!done && options.stopWhen?.({ step, carryover })) done = true;
115:     }
116: 
117:     if (!done && run.status === "completed" && run.chunks.length >= config.maxChunks) {
118:       run.status = "max-chunks";
119:     }
120:   } catch (err) {
121:     run.status = "errored";
122:     run.error = (err as Error).message;
123:     progress.phase("error", run.error);
124:   }
125: 
126:   run.output = cleanedParts.join("\n\n");
127:   const eff = runEfficiency(run.chunks, run.chunkConfig);
128:   run.totalTokensUsed = eff.totalTokensUsed;
129:   run.totalTokensSaved = eff.tokensSaved;
130:   run.efficiencyPercent = eff.efficiencyPercent;
131: 
132:   // Reflection: only on completed, non-aborted runs with chunks. Failure is non-fatal.
133:   if (options.reflect !== false && run.status === "completed" && run.chunks.length > 0) {
134:     progress.phase("reflecting");
135:     try {
136:       const codeBlocks = (run.output.match(/```/g)?.length ?? 0) / 2;
137:       const reflectionPrompt =
138:         `Reflect on this completed run.\nGoal: ${goal.slice(0, 200)}\nFinal state: ${carryover}\n` +
139:         `Output (truncated): ${run.output.slice(0, 4000)}\nCode blocks: ${Math.floor(codeBlocks)}\n` +
140:         `Verdict: ratify if the goal is met, refine with concrete gaps otherwise.`;
141:       const { text } = await generator(reflectionPrompt, [], "You are the reflection pass. Be brief and concrete.", undefined, options.abortSignal);
142:       run.reflection = cleanMarkers(text);
143:     } catch (err) {
144:       run.reflection = undefined;
145:       run.error = `reflection failed (run preserved): ${(err as Error).message}`;
146:     }
147:   }
148: 
149:   run.durationMs = clock() - start;
150:   progress.phase(run.status === "errored" ? "error" : "complete", run.status);
151:   return run;
152: }
153: 
154: // The examples use a simplified stepFn({goal, carryover, step}) shape; adapt
155: // it to the provider-agnostic Generator contract (section 12).
156: function normalizeGenerator(options: RunOptions, fallback: Generator | undefined, goal: string): Generator {
157:   if (options.generator) return options.generator;
158:   if (options.stepFn) {
159:     const stepFn: StepFn = options.stepFn;
160:     let step = 0; // 0-based for the stepFn contract used across the examples
161:     return async (prompt) => {
162:       const result = await stepFn({ goal, carryover: extractCarryoverFromPrompt(prompt), step, prompt });
163:       step += 1;
164:       return { text: result.content };
165:     };
166:   }
167:   if (fallback) return fallback;
168:   throw new Error("Markovian: provide a generator or stepFn");
169: }
170: 
171: function extractCarryoverFromPrompt(prompt: string): string {
172:   const m = prompt.match(/\[CARRYOVER STATE\]\n([\s\S]*?)(?:\n\n|$)/);
173:   return m ? m[1].trim() : "";
174: }

68:     for (const run of this.runs) {

70:       stats.totalTokensUsed += eff.totalTokensUsed;

72:       stats.totalChunksProcessed += run.chunks.length;
73:       stats.lastRunTimestamp = Math.max(stats.lastRunTimestamp, run.timestamp);
74:       stats.efficiencyHistory.push({ timestamp: run.timestamp, efficiency: eff.efficiencyPercent, tokensSaved: eff.tokensSaved });

43:     injection?: boolean;
44:     clarification?: boolean;
45:     reason?: string;
46:   };
47:   tags?: string[];
48: };

50: type Result = { ex: Example; out: any };
51: type Metrics = Record<string, number>;
52: 
53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
54: // Corpus loading
55: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56: 
57: function loadJsonl(path: string): Example[] {
58:   return readFileSync(path, "utf-8")
59:     .split("\n")
60:     .filter(Boolean)
61:     .map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
62: }
63: 
64: const FILTER_DIRS: Record<string, string[]> = {
65:   all: ["intents", "injection", "multi-intent", "edge-cases"],
66:   intent: ["intents"],
67:   injection: ["injection"],
68:   "multi-intent": ["multi-intent"],
69: };
70: 
71: function loadCorpus(version: string, filter: keyof typeof FILTER_DIRS = "all"): Example[] {
72:   const base = join(__dirname, "../regression-set", version);
73:   const dirs = FILTER_DIRS[filter] ?? FILTER_DIRS.all;
74:   const out: Example[] = [];
75:   for (const d of dirs) {
76:     try {
77:       for (const f of readdirSync(join(base, d))) {
78:         if (f.endsWith(".jsonl")) out.push(...loadJsonl(join(base, d, f)));
79:       }
80:     } catch {}
81:   }
82:   return out;
83: }
84: 
85: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
86: // Scout implementation loading (this repo ships the spec, not the code)
87: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
88: 
89: async function loadScout(): Promise<any> {
90:   const implPath = process.env.SCOUT_IMPL;
91:   if (!implPath) {
92:     console.error(
93:       [
94:         "SCOUT_IMPL is not set.",
95:         "",
96:         "This repository is the Scout implementation spec: src/ is intentionally",
97:         "empty and @meterless/scout is not published. To run the harness, point",
98:         "SCOUT_IMPL at a module exporting a spec-compatible `Scout` class:",
99:         "",
100:         "  SCOUT_IMPL=/abs/path/to/your/scout/index.js npm run evals",
101:         "",
102:         "See docs/architecture.md and docs/eval-harness.md for the required API.",
103:       ].join("\n"),
104:     );
105:     process.exit(2);
106:   }
107:   // Windows absolute paths must be imported as file:// URLs.
108:   const { pathToFileURL } = await import("node:url");
109:   const mod = await import(pathToFileURL(implPath).href);
110:   if (typeof mod.Scout !== "function") {
111:     console.error(`SCOUT_IMPL module "${implPath}" does not export a Scout class.`);
112:     process.exit(2);
113:   }
114:   return new mod.Scout({
115:     intentRegistry: join(__dirname, "../fixtures/intents.json"),
116:     policyPack: ["default", "adversarial-tight"],
117:   });
118: }
119: 
120: async function runOne(scout: any, ex: Example) {
121:   return scout.decide({
122:     prompt: ex.prompt,
123:     user: { id: "eval", role: ex.user?.role ?? "ae" },
124:     surface: ex.surface ?? "chat",
125:   });
126: }
127: 
128: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
129: // Metric computation (aggregate + per-slice)
130: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
131: 
132: type Tally = {
133:   intentTop1Hits: number;
134:   intentTop3Hits: number;
135:   intentTotal: number;
136:   injTP: number;
137:   injFP: number;
138:   injFN: number;
139:   injTN: number;
140:   toolHits: number;
141:   toolTotal: number;
142:   clarifications: number;
143:   contractsIssued: number;
144:   overrides: number;
145:   overrideDataSeen: boolean;
146:   n: number;
147: };
148: 
149: function tally(results: Result[]): Tally {
150:   const t: Tally = {
151:     intentTop1Hits: 0, intentTop3Hits: 0, intentTotal: 0,
152:     injTP: 0, injFP: 0, injFN: 0, injTN: 0,
153:     toolHits: 0, toolTotal: 0,
154:     clarifications: 0,
155:     contractsIssued: 0, overrides: 0, overrideDataSeen: false,
156:     n: results.length,
157:   };
158: 
159:   for (const { ex, out } of results) {
160:     // Intent metrics — top-1 = executionContract.intent.primary.id,
161:     // top-3 from candidates.slice(0, 3).
162:     if (ex.expected.intent) {
163:       t.intentTotal++;
164:       const top1 = out.executionContract?.intent?.primary?.id;
165:       const top3 = (out.candidates ?? []).slice(0, 3).map((c: any) => c.intent);
166:       if (top1 === ex.expected.intent) t.intentTop1Hits++;
167:       if (top3.includes(ex.expected.intent)) t.intentTop3Hits++;
168:     }
169: 
170:     // Injection metrics — detected ⇔ risk.level === "block".
171:     if (ex.expected.injection !== undefined) {
172:       const blocked = out.risk?.level === "block";
173:       if (ex.expected.injection && blocked) t.injTP++;
174:       else if (ex.expected.injection && !blocked) t.injFN++;
175:       else if (!ex.expected.injection && blocked) t.injFP++;
176:       else t.injTN++;
177:     }
178: 
179:     // Tool precision — expected plan ⊆ emitted plan capabilities.
180:     if (ex.expected.toolPlan?.length) {
181:       t.toolTotal++;
182:       const got = (out.toolPlan ?? []).map((s: any) => s.capability);
183:       if (ex.expected.toolPlan.every((c) => got.includes(c))) t.toolHits++;
184:     }
185: 
186:     if (out.clarification) t.clarifications++;
187: 
188:     // Override frequency — user corrections ("No, I meant…" + intent switch
189:     // within the same trace) ÷ contracts issued. In offline eval runs the
190:     // implementation may replay recorded overrides on `out.overrides`.
191:     if (out.executionContract) t.contractsIssued++;
192:     if (out.overrides !== undefined) {
193:       t.overrideDataSeen = true;
194:       t.overrides += Array.isArray(out.overrides) ? out.overrides.length : 0;
195:     }
196:   }
197:   return t;
198: }
199: 
200: function toMetrics(t: Tally): Metrics {
201:   return {
202:     intent_top1: t.intentTotal ? t.intentTop1Hits / t.intentTotal : 0,
203:     intent_top3_recall: t.intentTotal ? t.intentTop3Hits / t.intentTotal : 0,
204:     injection_precision: t.injTP + t.injFP ? t.injTP / (t.injTP + t.injFP) : 1,
205:     injection_recall: t.injTP + t.injFN ? t.injTP / (t.injTP + t.injFN) : 1,
206:     tool_precision: t.toolTotal ? t.toolHits / t.toolTotal : 0,
207:     clarification_rate: t.n ? t.clarifications / t.n : 0,
208:     override_frequency: t.contractsIssued ? t.overrides / t.contractsIssued : 0,
209:   };
210: }
211: 
212: /** Which slice value an example belongs to, per dimension in thresholds.yaml. */
213: function sliceValue(ex: Example, dim: string): string | undefined {
214:   switch (dim) {
215:     case "surface": return ex.surface ?? "chat";
216:     case "role": return ex.user?.role ?? "ae";
217:     case "intent_family": return ex.expected.intent?.split(".")[0];
218:     case "risk_class":
219:       return ex.expected.risk && ex.expected.risk !== "block" ? ex.expected.risk : undefined;
220:     default: return undefined;
221:   }
222: }
223: 
224: type SliceReport = Record<string, { metrics: Metrics; tally: Tally }>;
225: 
226: function computeSlices(results: Result[], thresholds: any): SliceReport {
227:   const slices: SliceReport = {};
228:   for (const spec of thresholds.slices ?? []) {
229:     const dim: string = spec.dim;
230:     for (const value of spec.values ?? []) {
231:       const subset = results.filter((r) => sliceValue(r.ex, dim) === value);
232:       if (!subset.length) continue; // no examples in this slice for corpus v1
233:       const t = tally(subset);
234:       slices[`${dim}=${value}`] = { metrics: toMetrics(t), tally: t };
235:     }
236:   }
237:   return slices;
238: }
239: 
240: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
241: // Gating
242: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
243: 
244: function gate(
245:   metrics: Metrics,
246:   slices: SliceReport,
247:   thresholds: any,
248: ): { pass: boolean; failures: string[] } {
249:   const failures: string[] = [];
250: 
251:   for (const [name, t] of Object.entries(thresholds.metrics as Record<string, any>)) {
252:     const v = metrics[name];
253:     if (v === undefined) continue;
254:     if (t.hard_floor !== undefined && v < t.hard_floor)
255:       failures.push(`${name}=${v.toFixed(3)} below floor ${t.hard_floor}`);
256:     if (t.hard_max !== undefined && v > t.hard_max)
257:       failures.push(`${name}=${v.toFixed(3)} above ceiling ${t.hard_max}`);
258:   }
259: 
260:   // Per-slice hard floors (slice_policy). A global pass with a failing slice
261:   // is a failure. Only slices that actually contain relevant examples gate.
262:   for (const [metric, policy] of Object.entries((thresholds.slice_policy ?? {}) as Record<string, any>)) {
263:     const floor = policy.slice_hard_floor;
264:     if (floor === undefined) continue;
265:     for (const [key, s] of Object.entries(slices)) {
266:       const relevant =
267:         metric === "intent_top1" ? s.tally.intentTotal > 0 :
268:         metric === "injection_precision" ? s.tally.injTP + s.tally.injFP > 0 :
269:         true;
270:       if (!relevant) continue;
271:       const v = s.metrics[metric];
272:       if (v !== undefined && v < floor)
273:         failures.push(`slice ${key}: ${metric}=${v.toFixed(3)} below slice floor ${floor}`);
274:     }
275:   }
276: 
277:   return { pass: failures.length === 0, failures };
278: }
279: 
280: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
281: // Reporting
282: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
283: 
284: function writeReport(
285:   metrics: Metrics,
286:   slices: SliceReport,
287:   notes: string[],
288:   gateResult: { pass: boolean; failures: string[] },
289:   corpusSize: number,
290:   outPath: string,
291: ) {
292:   const lines = [
293:     "# Scout eval report\n",
294:     `_Generated: ${new Date().toISOString()} · corpus v1 · ${corpusSize} examples_\n`,
295:     `## Verdict: ${gateResult.pass ? "✅ PASS" : "❌ FAIL"}\n`,
296:   ];
297:   if (!gateResult.pass) {
298:     lines.push("### Failures\n");
299:     for (const f of gateResult.failures) lines.push(`- ${f}`);
300:     lines.push("");
301:   }
302:   lines.push("## Metrics\n\n| metric | value |\n|---|---|");
303:   for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(metrics)) lines.push(`| ${k} | ${v.toFixed(3)} |`);
304: 
305:   lines.push("\n## Slices\n\n| slice | intent_top1 | injection_precision | n |\n|---|---|---|---|");
306:   for (const [key, s] of Object.entries(slices)) {
307:     const it = s.tally.intentTotal > 0 ? s.metrics.intent_top1.toFixed(3) : "—";
308:     const ip = s.tally.injTP + s.tally.injFP > 0 ? s.metrics.injection_precision.toFixed(3) : "—";
309:     lines.push(`| ${key} | ${it} | ${ip} | ${s.tally.n} |`);
310:   }
311: 
312:   if (notes.length) {
313:     lines.push("\n## Notes\n");
314:     for (const n of notes) lines.push(`- ${n}`);
315:   }
316:   writeFileSync(outPath, lines.join("\n"));
317:   console.log(`Report written: ${outPath}`);
318: }
319: 
320: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
321: // Main
322: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
323: 
324: async function main() {
325:   const filter = (process.argv[2] as keyof typeof FILTER_DIRS) ?? "all";
326:   const thresholds = parseYaml(readFileSync(join(__dirname, "../config/thresholds.yaml"), "utf-8"));
327:   const corpus = loadCorpus("v1", filter);
328:   console.log(`Loaded ${corpus.length} examples from v1/${filter}`);
329: 
330:   const scout = await loadScout();
331: 
332:   const results: Result[] = [];
333:   for (const ex of corpus) {
334:     try {
335:       const out = await runOne(scout, ex);
336:       results.push({ ex, out });
337:     } catch (err) {
338:       console.warn(`Skipped ${ex.id}: ${(err as Error).message}`);
339:     }
340:   }
341: 
342:   const t = tally(results);
343:   const metrics = toMetrics(t);
344:   const slices = computeSlices(results, thresholds);
345: 
346:   const notes: string[] = [];
347:   if (!t.overrideDataSeen) {
348:     notes.push(
349:       "override_frequency = 0.000 by definition of the corpus, not by measurement: " +
350:         "no override data in corpus v1. Overrides are user corrections captured in " +
351:         "telemetry (\"No, I meant…\" + intent switch within the same trace) ÷ contracts " +
352:         "issued — measure this in production telemetry (docs/telemetry-and-learning.md).",
353:     );
354:   }
355: 
356:   const gateResult = gate(metrics, slices, thresholds);
357: 
358:   mkdirSync(join(__dirname, "../reports"), { recursive: true });
359:   writeReport(metrics, slices, notes, gateResult, corpus.length, join(__dirname, "../reports/latest.md"));
360: 
361:   console.table(metrics);
362:   for (const n of notes) console.log(`note: ${n}`);
363:   if (!gateResult.pass) {
364:     console.error("\n❌ Eval gate failed:");
365:     for (const f of gateResult.failures) console.error(`  - ${f}`);
366:     process.exit(1);
367:   }
368: }
369: 
370: main();

1: # Scout Intent Agnostic Implementation Guide
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document codifies a production implementation of Scout, the intent detection, risk guarding, and routing engine that runs BEFORE every meaningful action an agentic system takes. It is expressed in platform-neutral terms so any product can implement the same architecture as modular services.
6: 
7: It covers:
8: 
9: - The five-stage decision pipeline (Sense, Interpret, Guard, Route, Recommend)
10: - The intent registry contract and versioning
11: - Two-stage scoring with the canonical confidence formula and bands
12: - The guard stack (injection, policy, scope, sensitivity, rate limits)
13: - The capability graph and tool-plan assembly
14: - Model profile routing
15: - The signed execution contract, the only artifact downstream engines accept
16: - Telemetry, the learning loop, and the eval gates that ship releases
17: 
18: Every number in this guide is traceable to a file in `docs/`. Where the docs leave a choice open, it is marked `(implementer's choice)`.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1) Core Design Principles
23: 
24: - **Nothing acts on a raw prompt.** Downstream engines (H-MEM, World Model, Markovian, Swarm) act only on signed execution contracts.
25: - **If an intent is not in the registry, it cannot be acted on.** The registry is the system's entire surface area; this is the property that prevents scope drift.
26: - **Deterministic floor, optional intelligence.** Stage-1 scoring is pure rules and always available; Stage-2 model rescoring is an upgrade, never a dependency.
27: - **Refuse at the boundary.** Scope violations are refused by the executor verifying the contract, not politely discouraged by a wrapper.
28: - **Clarify when unsure, but clarification is a cost.** The clarification rate has a hard ceiling in the eval gates; a system that always asks fails that gate.
29: - **Every decision is replayable.** Contracts carry trace IDs; telemetry reconstructs any decision after the fact.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2) The Pipeline
34: 
35: Five stages, in order, per request:
36: 
37: ```
38: Sense -> Interpret -> Guard -> Route -> Recommend -> ExecutionContract
39: ```
40: 
41: 1. **Sense** classifies intent from raw input. Output: top-k scored candidates, never a single label.
42: 2. **Interpret** binds parameters and entity references from the prompt to the top intent, and decides whether clarification is needed.
43: 3. **Guard** runs the policy stack. Output: risk level `low | medium | high | block` plus flags, redactions, and a reason on block.
44: 4. **Route** walks the capability graph to assemble a tool plan.
45: 5. **Recommend** picks the model profile and bundles everything into a signed contract.
46: 
47: The pipeline's public surface (see `docs/architecture.md` quickstart):
48: 
49: ```ts
50: class Scout {
51:   constructor(options: {
52:     intentRegistry: string | IntentRegistry;   // file path or composed registry
53:     policyPack?: string;                        // named policy set, default "default"
54:     modelProfiles?: string;                     // profiles file
55:   });
56: 
57:   // Full pipeline: returns { intent, risk, executionContract, ... }
58:   decide(input: { prompt: string; user?: UserRef; surface: string; context?: unknown }): Promise<Decision>;
59: 
60:   // Sense stage only: returns { candidates: { intent, score }[] }
61:   classify(input: { prompt: string; surface: string }): Promise<{ candidates: IntentCandidate[] }>;
62: 
63:   // Re-planning with lineage (section 8)
64:   replan(input: { parent: string; reason: string; state?: unknown }): Promise<Decision>;
65: }
66: ```
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 3) Intent Registry (the catalog)
71: 
72: Canonical record shape (`docs/intent-registry.md`):
73: 
74: ```ts
75: type Intent = {
76:   id: string;                    // "deal.recover"; category.name grammar
77:   category: string;              // "deal", "email", "research"
78:   description: string;           // doubles as the classifier prompt
79:   parameters: ParameterSchema;   // JSON-schema-style, validated at Interpret
80:   capabilities: CapabilityRef[]; // abstract verbs, resolved by the graph
81:   riskClass: "low" | "medium" | "high";
82:   surfaces: string[];            // where this intent may be invoked
83:   roles: string[];               // who may invoke it
84:   examples: string[];            // classifier seeds AND eval fixtures; mandatory
85:   version: number;               // bump on ANY change; triggers re-eval
86: };
87: ```
88: 
89: Rules:
90: 
91: - Examples are mandatory. An intent without examples cannot be classified or evaluated.
92: - Base `riskClass` sets the policy floor; risk is re-evaluated per request but never below the floor.
93: - `surfaces` and `roles` are enforced at Guard; a viewer-role invocation of an AE-only intent blocks before classification returns.
94: - The registry carries a `registryVersion`, stamped on every contract, so downstream engines detect drift.
95: - Loaders: single JSON file, directory of per-intent files, or composition of registries.
96: 
97: Scale reference: the canonical Meterless runtime registry ships 131 intents (31 foundation + 100 expansion) plus 8 topology vectors (`pipeline`, `fan_out`, `debate`, `loop`, `hierarchical`, `star`, `tree`, `mesh`) emitted as `scout_topology_pattern` for orchestrator DAG selection. The registries in this folder's `evals/fixtures/` and examples are deliberately small teaching registries (3-13 intents); do not mistake them for the production catalog.
98: 
99: Anti-patterns: one giant do-anything intent (that is `if (true)`, not Scout); an intent per minor variation (parameterize instead); capabilities embedded in intent logic (they belong in the graph).
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## 4) Scoring (Sense stage)
104: 
105: Two execution stages, one canonical formula (`docs/scoring.md`).
106: 
107: ### 4.1 Stage 1: deterministic trigger scan
108: 
109: - Weighted trigger-word/substring scan over the FULL registry. Pure rules, no model call.
110: - Winner = highest weighted-match sum; confidence = winner's score as a fraction of matched weight.
111: - Hard latency budget: a full-registry scan completes in under 16 ms, enforced by a startup self-test over a fixed probe set that fails loudly when exceeded.
112: - Runs on every keystroke (UI feedback) and on submit (routing).
113: 
114: ### 4.2 Stage 2: hybrid rescoring (optional, recommended for routing)
115: 
116: - Small local classifier (embedding model, 50-200 MB, ONNX/WebLLM class) adds semantic similarity.
117: - Conversation window, active workflow, and retrieved memory add the contextual term.
118: - If Stage 2 is unavailable (no model, cold start), Stage 1's result stands. Graceful degradation, never a hard dependency.
119: 
120: ### 4.3 The canonical formula
121: 
122: ```
123: finalScore(intent) =
124:   0.40 * lexical(intent)      // trigger phrases, synonyms, n-grams
125: + 0.35 * semantic(intent)     // embedding similarity vs intent prototypes
126: + 0.20 * contextual(intent)   // recent turns, active workflow, retrieved memory
127: + 0.05 * recency(intent)      // used recently in-session
128: - riskPenalty(intent)         // down-rank intents requesting blocked actions
129: ```
130: 
131: Stage 1 alone yields `lexical` and `recency`; `semantic` and `contextual` default to 0 until Stage 2 runs. The merge is a single dot product. All weights are config data, not code, tunable per surface.
132: 
133: ### 4.4 Confidence bands (the load-bearing numbers)
134: 
135: | Band | Range | Action |
136: |---|---|---|
137: | High | >= 0.80 | Proceed. Direct routing. |
138: | Medium | 0.55 - 0.79 | Proceed and log for review; offer "did you mean?" inline |
139: | Low | 0.40 - 0.54 | Ask for clarification; offer top-3 as options |
140: | Reject | < 0.40 | Fall back to the safe `GENERAL` intent; explain; never guess a high-risk intent |
141: 
142: Bands are configurable per surface (tighten for high-risk, loosen for low-risk), but these are the canonical defaults and the values the examples and evals assume.
143: 
144: ### 4.5 Multi-intent
145: 
146: When two candidates are both in the High band and reference disjoint spans of the prompt, return a plan containing both intents rather than choosing. Secondary intents are everything at or above 0.55 (the Medium floor). Each candidate carries its `span`.
147: 
148: ### 4.6 Clarification triggers
149: 
150: Emit a structured clarification (question plus up to 4 options, each mapping to an intent) when ANY of:
151: 
152: 1. Top-1 score is in the Low band (0.40 - 0.54).
153: 2. Top-1 and top-2 are within 0.05 of each other in the Medium band.
154: 3. Required parameters cannot be bound from the prompt.
155: 4. The intent is risk-class `high` and confidence is below 0.95.
156: 
157: Clarification rate is a tracked metric with a hard ceiling (section 10).
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 5) Interpret Stage
162: 
163: - Bind `parameters` per the intent's schema; coerce and validate types and ranges.
164: - Bind `references` (entities) from the prompt and context to stable IDs; unresolved required references trigger clarification rule 3.
165: - Attach `alternates`: the remaining top-k candidates with scores, so downstream surfaces can offer corrections.
166: - Output feeds Guard unchanged; Interpret never mutates scores.
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ## 6) Guard Stage (risk and policy)
171: 
172: Five independent layers (`docs/risk-and-policy.md`), each returning `pass | warn | block` plus a structured reason:
173: 
174: 1. **Injection check.** Multi-layered: known-pattern match (role-confusion markers, embedded control like `</system>`, `[INST]`), role-drift detection, out-of-band tool references (asking for tools not reachable from the current intent's capability set), and an optional small model check. Output includes `kind`, `score`, and `evidence`. Detected injection payloads are NOT logged in full by default; metadata only `(configurable per deployment)`.
175: 2. **Policy gate.** RBAC plus declarative per-intent policy files: allowed roles and surfaces, parameter bounds, denied parameter combinations, and `require-approval` conditions.
176: 3. **Scope check.** Does this intent fit this user, this surface, this session? Registry `surfaces`/`roles` are the floor.
177: 4. **PII / sensitivity.** Redact or block by data class; redactions are recorded on the contract.
178: 5. **Rate limit.** Per user, per intent, per surface `(implementer's choice of limits)`.
179: 
180: Aggregate output: `{ level: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "block", flags, redactions, reason? }`. Any layer's `block` blocks; `warn`s escalate the level. High-risk intents additionally require approval records (section 8).
181: 
182: ---
183: 
184: ## 7) Route Stage (capability graph)
185: 
186: Intents declare abstract capabilities (`world.query`, `memory.recall`, `swarm.run`, `email.send`); the graph maps each to concrete tools at runtime (`docs/capability-graph.md`). Edges carry availability, latency, cost, and permission annotations.
187: 
188: Selection rules, in priority order:
189: 
190: 1. Required permissions: drop tools the user cannot use.
191: 2. Availability: drop offline or rate-limited tools.
192: 3. Surface preference: chat prefers conversational tools, inbox prefers email-first.
193: 4. Cost/latency budget: cheapest tool that meets the latency target.
194: 5. Tie-break: prefer local tools over remote. Local-first is the default.
195: 
196: Output is the ordered `toolPlan: { tool, input }[]`. A capability with no resolvable tool fails routing; the decision either degrades (drop optional steps) or triggers re-planning, never silently substitutes an out-of-scope tool.
197: 
198: ---
199: 
200: ## 8) Recommend Stage and the Execution Contract
201: 
202: ### 8.1 Model routing
203: 
204: Model profiles declare provider, model, context, cost, latency p95, capabilities, and cleared `dataClasses` (`docs/model-routing.md`). The router scores profiles per task: compatibility (function calling, JSON mode, vision) is mandatory; the profile must be cleared for the input's data class; then cost/latency budgets pick among survivors. Sensitive data classes route to local profiles.
205: 
206: ### 8.2 The contract (the only thing downstream engines accept)
207: 
208: Shape per `docs/execution-contract.md`:
209: 
210: ```ts
211: type ExecutionContract = {
212:   contractId: string;            // ULID, monotonic
213:   parentId?: string;             // re-planning lineage
214:   traceId: string;               // telemetry correlation
215:   intent: { primary, parameters, references, confidence, alternates };
216:   risk: { level, flags, redactions, approvals };
217:   toolPlan: ToolStep[];
218:   modelProfile: ModelProfileRef;
219:   scope: { user, surface, capabilities, deadline?, budget? };
220:   issuedAt: ISODate;
221:   expiresAt: ISODate;            // default TTL: 5 minutes
222:   registryVersion: number;
223:   policyPackVersion: string;
224:   signature: string;             // HMAC_SHA256(secret, canonical_json(contract_without_signature))
225:   signedBy: "scout";
226: };
227: ```
228: 
229: Hard rules:
230: 
231: - **Signature is mandatory at every boundary, including dev.** Downstream engines verify on receipt and refuse unsigned or tampered contracts. HMAC over the canonical JSON encoding is an integrity check, not cryptographic-grade defense; the signer interface is pluggable for stronger schemes.
232: - **Contracts expire; default TTL 5 minutes.** Engines refuse contracts past `expiresAt`. Never extend TTL; long-running work refreshes contracts per chunk/phase with the original as `parentId`.
233: - **Contracts are immutable post-signature.** Adding fields downstream means re-issuing.
234: - **Scope is enforced by the executor.** Every tool invoked downstream must be inside the contract's `capabilities` set; out-of-scope calls are refused at the executor boundary and logged as `contract.refused`.
235: - **High-risk contracts carry approval records** (`user-confirm`, `operator-review`); engines verify required approvals before acting.
236: - **Contracts are a handoff format, not a database.** Persist telemetry; do not build the system of record out of contracts.
237: 
238: ### 8.3 Re-planning
239: 
240: When a downstream engine cannot fulfill a step (tool offline, verification failed, threshold tightened), it calls `scout.replan({ parent, reason, state })`. The new contract shares the trace ID; telemetry tracks the chain.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## 9) Telemetry and Learning
245: 
246: Structured events at minimum (`docs/telemetry-and-learning.md`, `docs/execution-contract.md`):
247: 
248: ```
249: scout.decision       traceId=... intent=... band=... latencyMs=... stage2=used|skipped
250: contract.issued      contractId=... intent=... risk=... profile=...
251: contract.verified    contractId=... engine=...
252: contract.expired     contractId=... engine=...
253: contract.refused     contractId=... engine=... reason=scope-mismatch
254: scout.clarification  traceId=... trigger=low-band|tie|params|high-risk
255: scout.override       traceId=... from=... to=...   // user corrected the routing
256: ```
257: 
258: The learning loop: every clarification, override, and operator correction is logged; the training set updates nightly; the classifier retrains weekly; the new model passes the eval gates before shipping. Telemetry answers "why did the system do that" for any past decision via trace ID.
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ## 10) Eval Gates (metrics gate releases)
263: 
264: The eval harness (`evals/`, `docs/eval-harness.md`) runs the regression set against any implementation and scores per metric and per slice. Canonical thresholds (`evals/config/thresholds.yaml`):
265: 
266: | Metric | Target | Hard floor/ceiling |
267: |---|---|---|
268: | intent_top1 | 0.92 | floor 0.85 |
269: | intent_top3_recall | 0.98 | floor 0.94 |
270: | injection_precision | 0.95 | floor 0.90 |
271: | injection_recall | 0.90 | floor 0.82 |
272: | tool_precision | 0.88 | floor 0.80 |
273: | clarification_rate | max 0.15 | hard max 0.25 |
274: | override_frequency | max 0.08 | hard max 0.15 |
275: 
276: Slice floors prevent aggregate numbers from hiding a tanked slice: intent_top1 has a per-slice hard floor of 0.80 and injection_precision 0.85, sliced by surface, role, intent family, and risk class. Threshold changes require their own PR with historical comparison.
277: 
278: ---
279: 
280: ## 11) Suggested Service Boundaries
281: 
282: - `IntentRegistryService` (load, compose, validate, version)
283: - `ScoringService` (Stage-1 scanner with the startup self-test; Stage-2 rescorer; merge)
284: - `InterpretService` (parameter/reference binding, clarification decisions)
285: - `GuardService` (the five-layer stack, policy packs)
286: - `CapabilityGraphService` (graph, availability, tool-plan assembly)
287: - `ModelRouterService` (profiles, data classes, budgets)
288: - `ContractService` (issue, sign, verify, expire, replan lineage)
289: - `TelemetryService` (events, decision replay, learning-loop exports)
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## 12) Operational Defaults (Recommended)
294: 
295: - Confidence bands: High >= 0.80, Medium 0.55-0.79, Low 0.40-0.54, Reject < 0.40
296: - Formula weights: 0.40 lexical / 0.35 semantic / 0.20 contextual / 0.05 recency, minus riskPenalty
297: - Medium-band tie window for clarification: 0.05
298: - High-risk proceed threshold: 0.95
299: - Secondary-intent floor (multi-intent plans): 0.55
300: - Stage-1 full-registry scan budget: 16 ms, self-tested at startup
301: - Contract TTL: 5 minutes
302: - Clarification options per prompt: max 4
303: - Stage-2 classifier: 50-200 MB local embedding model; 20-80 ms client-side typical
304: 
305: ---
306: 
307: ## 13) Implementation Checklist
308: 
309: - Define the intent registry schema, loaders, and versioning.
310: - Implement the Stage-1 trigger scanner with the 16 ms startup self-test.
311: - Implement Stage-2 rescoring behind an availability check; merge with the canonical weights.
312: - Implement bands, multi-intent span detection, and the four clarification triggers.
313: - Implement Interpret: schema-validated parameter binding and entity references.
314: - Implement the five-layer guard stack with structured pass/warn/block output.
315: - Implement the capability graph with the five selection rules and local-first tie-break.
316: - Implement model profiles with data-class clearance.
317: - Implement the contract: canonical encoding, HMAC signing, TTL, verification, replan lineage.
318: - Emit the telemetry events; wire the learning-loop exports.
319: - Run the eval harness; ship only above the thresholds.
320: 
321: ---
322: 
323: ## 14) Explicit Non-Goals
324: 
325: - Scout does not execute anything. It decides, guards, routes, and signs. Executors execute.
326: - No provider lock-in: Stage-2 models, signers, and tools are all pluggable interfaces.
327: - No UI assumptions: clarifications and telemetry are structured data; surfaces render them.
328: 
329: ---
330: 
331: ## Verify your implementation
332: 
333: This engine ships its verification harness. After implementing, point the eval runner at your build and iterate until the thresholds pass:
334: 
335: ```bash
336: npm install
337: SCOUT_IMPL=/abs/path/to/your/scout/index.js npm run evals
338: ```
339: 
340: The runner (`evals/runner/`) loads the regression set (`evals/regression-set/v1/`), runs each example through your `Scout` (constructor options `{ intentRegistry, policyPack }`, async `decide()`), and reports per-metric scores and per-slice breakdowns against `evals/config/thresholds.yaml`. A release-quality implementation clears every hard floor and ceiling. To dispute a threshold, open an engine-spec-feedback issue with historical comparison.

15:   "node", "docker", "graphql", "redis", "webrtc", "tauri", "electron", "llm", "embedding",

19:   work: ["meeting", "deadline", "client", "project", "sprint", "review", "report"],

38: export class MemoryStoreService {

43:   constructor(

48:   ) {

159:   classifyDomain(content: string, tags: string[], type: MemoryType): string {
160:     for (const t of tags) {
161:       if (t.startsWith("project:")) return t.slice("project:".length);
162:       if (t.startsWith("tech:")) return "tech";
163:     }
164:     const tokens = new Set(tokenize(content));
165:     let best = "general";
166:     let bestScore = 0;
167:     for (const [domain, kws] of Object.entries(DOMAIN_KEYWORDS)) {
168:       let score = kws.reduce((s, kw) => s + (tokens.has(kw) ? 1 : 0), 0);
169:       if (domain === "personal" && (type === "personal" || type === "preference")) score += 1;
170:       if (score > bestScore) {
171:         best = domain;
172:         bestScore = score;
173:       }
174:     }
175:     return bestScore > 0 ? best : "general";

178:   private namespace(domain: string, type: MemoryType): string {
179:     const bucket = type === "preference" || type === "personal" ? "profile" : type === "factual" ? "facts" : "notes";
180:     return `${domain}/${bucket}`;

183:   extractEntities(content: string): string[] {
184:     const entities = new Set<string>();
185:     for (const t of tokenize(content)) if (TECH_TERMS.includes(t)) entities.add(t);
186:     for (const m of content.matchAll(/\b([A-Z][a-zA-Z]{2,})\b/g)) {
187:       const norm = m[1].toLowerCase();

193:   private discoverRelationships(record: MemoryRecord): void {
194:     const CORRECTION = /\b(actually|instead|no longer|not anymore|changed to|correction)\b/i;
195:     for (const other of this.records.values()) {
196:       if (record.relatedTo.length >= DEFAULTS.relatedCap) break;
197:       const sharedEntities = other.entities.filter((e) => record.entities.includes(e));
198:       const sim = cosine(record.embedding, other.embedding);
199:       if (!record.supersedes && sim > 0.85 && CORRECTION.test(record.content)) {
200:         record.supersedes = other.id;

202:       }
203:       if (sharedEntities.length >= 1 && other.domain === record.domain) {
204:         record.relatedTo.push(other.id);
205:         if (other.relatedTo.length < DEFAULTS.relatedCap && !other.relatedTo.includes(record.id)) {
206:           other.relatedTo.push(record.id); // bidirectional link
207:         }
208:       }
209:     }
210:   }
211: }

214:   const { embedding, ...rest } = structuredClone(r);

1: // Deterministic mock embedder: FNV-1a hash per token into a 64-dim vector,
2: // summed and L2-normalized. Pure function of the input text, so retrieval
3: // scores are reproducible across runs and machines. Swap in a real provider
4: // by replacing embed() in your own implementation; the contract is just
5: // text -> number[].
6: 
7: const DIM = 64;
8: 
9: export function tokenize(text: string): string[] {
10:   return text
11:     .toLowerCase()
12:     .replace(/[^a-z0-9\s]/g, " ")
13:     .split(/\s+/)
14:     .filter((t) => t.length > 1);
15: }
16: 
17: function fnv1a(str: string): number {
18:   let h = 0x811c9dc5;
19:   for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
20:     h ^= str.charCodeAt(i);
21:     h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193) >>> 0;
22:   }
23:   return h >>> 0;
24: }
25: 
26: export function embed(text: string): number[] {
27:   const vec = new Array<number>(DIM).fill(0);
28:   for (const token of tokenize(text)) {
29:     const h = fnv1a(token);
30:     const idx = h % DIM;
31:     const sign = (h >>> 8) % 2 === 0 ? 1 : -1;
32:     const mag = 1 + ((h >>> 16) % 8) / 8;
33:     vec[idx] += sign * mag;
34:   }
35:   const norm = Math.sqrt(vec.reduce((s, v) => s + v * v, 0));
36:   return norm === 0 ? vec : vec.map((v) => v / norm);
37: }
38: 
39: export function cosine(a: number[], b: number[]): number {
40:   let dot = 0;
41:   for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) dot += a[i] * b[i];
42:   return dot; // both vectors are unit-length
43: }
44: 
45: export function jaccard(a: Iterable<string>, b: Iterable<string>): number {
46:   const sa = new Set(a);
47:   const sb = new Set(b);
48:   if (sa.size === 0 || sb.size === 0) return 0;
49:   let inter = 0;
50:   for (const x of sa) if (sb.has(x)) inter++;
51:   return inter / (sa.size + sb.size - inter);
52: }

1: // Hybrid retrieval and reinjection (AGENTS.md section 6). The canonical formula:
2: //
3: //   raw = 0.35*semantic + 0.20*keyword + 0.10*tag + 0.10*domain
4: //       + 0.15*entity   + 0.05*layer   + 0.05*recency - 0.20*superseded
5: //   score = clamp01(raw) * confidence          <- confidence multiplies AFTER the sum
6: //
7: // keyword = Jaccard of the top-8 query tokens vs memory tokens.
8: // layer weights: long_term 1.0, working 0.8, short_term 0.6.
9: // recency = exponential decay on lastAccessed, 14-day time constant.
10: // superseded records are penalized, never deleted or filtered.
11: // Threshold 0.35 applies to the FINAL score; top N = 5.
12: 
13: import { DAY_MS, DEFAULTS, clamp01 } from "./types.ts";
14: import type { MemoryRecord, QueryResult, RetrievedMemory } from "./types.ts";
15: import { cosine, embed, jaccard, tokenize } from "./embeddings.ts";
16: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
17: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
18: import { FEEDBACK_DELTAS } from "./types.ts";
19: import type { FeedbackKind } from "./types.ts";
20: import { snapshot } from "./memoryStore.ts";
21: 
22: const LAYER_WEIGHT: Record<MemoryRecord["layer"], number> = {
23:   long_term: 1.0,
24:   working: 0.8,
25:   short_term: 0.6,
26: };
27: 
28: export class MemoryRetrievalService {
29:   constructor(
30:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
31:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
32:     private clock: () => number,
33:     private actor: string
34:   ) {}
35: 
36:   scoreOne(memory: MemoryRecord, query: string): number {
37:     const queryEmbedding = embed(query);
38:     const queryTokens = tokenize(query).slice(0, 8);
39:     const queryEntities = this.store.extractEntities(query);
40:     const queryDomain = this.store.classifyDomain(query, [], "general");
41:     return this.score(memory, queryEmbedding, queryTokens, queryEntities, queryDomain);
42:   }
43: 
44:   private score(
45:     m: MemoryRecord,
46:     queryEmbedding: number[],
47:     queryTokens: string[],
48:     queryEntities: string[],
49:     queryDomain: string
50:   ): number {
51:     const semantic = clamp01(cosine(queryEmbedding, m.embedding));
52:     const keyword = jaccard(queryTokens, tokenize(m.content));
53:     const tag = jaccard(queryTokens, m.tags.map((t) => t.toLowerCase()));
54:     const domain = m.domain === queryDomain ? 1 : 0;
55:     const entity = jaccard(queryEntities, m.entities);
56:     const layer = LAYER_WEIGHT[m.layer];
57:     const ageDays = (this.clock() - m.lastAccessed) / DAY_MS;
58:     const recency = Math.exp(-ageDays / DEFAULTS.recencyDays);
59:     const superseded = m.supersededBy ? 1 : 0;
60:     const raw =
61:       0.35 * semantic + 0.2 * keyword + 0.1 * tag + 0.1 * domain +
62:       0.15 * entity + 0.05 * layer + 0.05 * recency - 0.2 * superseded;
63:     return clamp01(raw) * m.confidence;
64:   }
65: 
66:   query(query: string, opts?: { topN?: number; threshold?: number; chatId?: string }): QueryResult {
67:     const queryEmbedding = embed(query);
68:     const queryTokens = tokenize(query).slice(0, 8);
69:     const queryEntities = this.store.extractEntities(query);
70:     const queryDomain = this.store.classifyDomain(query, [], "general");
71:     const threshold = opts?.threshold ?? DEFAULTS.retrievalThreshold;
72:     const topN = opts?.topN ?? DEFAULTS.retrievalTopN;
73: 
74:     const scored: RetrievedMemory[] = [];
75:     for (const m of this.store.all()) {
76:       if (opts?.chatId && m.chatId && m.chatId !== opts.chatId) continue;
77:       const s = this.score(m, queryEmbedding, queryTokens, queryEntities, queryDomain);
78:       if (s >= threshold) scored.push({ memory: m, relevance: s });
79:     }
80:     scored.sort((a, b) => b.relevance - a.relevance || a.memory.id.localeCompare(b.memory.id));
81:     const top = scored.slice(0, topN);
82: 
83:     for (const { memory } of top) {
84:       this.store.touch(memory.id);
85:       this.ledger.log(memory.id, "read", this.actor, { details: { query } });
86:     }
87: 
88:     const strategy = top.length <= 1 ? "minimal" : top.some((t) => t.memory.type === "personal" || t.memory.type === "preference") ? "personal" : "comprehensive";
89:     return {
90:       memories: top,
91:       context: this.formatReinjection(top),
92:       trace: {
93:         retrievalReason: `hybrid ranking for "${query}" (domain: ${queryDomain})`,
94:         strategy,
95:         scores: Object.fromEntries(top.map((t) => [t.memory.id, Number(t.relevance.toFixed(4))])),
96:       },
97:     };
98:   }
99: 
100:   // Domain-grouped reinjection blocks with layer markers and entities (section 6.2).
101:   formatReinjection(items: RetrievedMemory[]): string {
102:     if (items.length === 0) return "";
103:     const byDomain = new Map<string, RetrievedMemory[]>();
104:     for (const it of items) {
105:       const list = byDomain.get(it.memory.domain) ?? [];
106:       list.push(it);
107:       byDomain.set(it.memory.domain, list);
108:     }
109:     const lines: string[] = ["[MEMORY CONTEXT]"];
110:     for (const [domain, list] of [...byDomain.entries()].sort()) {
111:       lines.push(`## ${domain}`);
112:       for (const { memory } of list) {
113:         const marker = memory.layer === "long_term" ? "LT" : memory.layer === "working" ? "WK" : "ST";
114:         const ents = memory.entities.length ? ` (entities: ${memory.entities.join(", ")})` : "";
115:         lines.push(`- [${marker}] ${memory.content}${ents} <${memory.id}>`);
116:       }
117:     }
118:     lines.push("[/MEMORY CONTEXT]");
119:     return lines.join("\n");
120:   }
121: 
122:   // Exact feedback deltas (AGENTS.md section 9.2).
123:   feedback(memoryId: string, kind: FeedbackKind): void {
124:     const m = this.store.get(memoryId);
125:     if (!m) throw new Error(`H-MEM: unknown memory id ${memoryId}`);
126:     const prev = snapshot(m);
127:     if (kind === "helpful") m.accessCount += 1;
128:     m.confidence = clamp01(m.confidence + FEEDBACK_DELTAS[kind]);
129:     if (kind === "wrong" && !m.tags.includes("review")) m.tags.push("review");
130:     this.ledger.log(memoryId, "feedback", this.actor, {
131:       previousState: prev,
132:       newState: snapshot(m),
133:       details: { kind, delta: FEEDBACK_DELTAS[kind] },
134:     });
135:     this.store.persist();
136:   }
137: }
