13:   file_save: "factual",
14:   file_open: "general",
15:   file_edit: "factual",
16:   model_response: "factual",
17:   plan_completion: "factual",
18: };
19: 
20: const SIGNAL = /\b(prefer|always|never|decided|chose|choose|use|because|instead|must|should|important|remember)\b/i;
21: 
22: export class MemoryMiningService {
23:   constructor(
24:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
25:     private clock: () => number,
26:     private minerFn?: (prompt: string) => Promise<string>
27:   ) {}
28: 
29:   async mineInteraction(event: MiningEventType, text: string, opts?: { chatId?: string; layer?: MemoryLayer }): Promise<MemoryRecord[]> {
30:     const candidates = this.minerFn
31:       ? await this.mineWithModel(event, text)
32:       : this.mineModelFree(text);
33:     return candidates.map((content) =>
34:       this.store.add({
35:         content,
36:         type: EVENT_TYPE_MAP[event],
37:         layer: opts?.layer ?? (this.minerFn ? "working" : "short_term"),
38:         tags: [`event:${event}`],
39:         source: `interaction:${event}`,
40:         provenance: { origin: event, learnedAt: this.clock(), label: `mined from ${event}` },
41:         chatId: opts?.chatId,
42:       })
43:     );
44:   }
45: 
46:   async mineDocument(fileName: string, text: string): Promise<MemoryRecord[]> {
47:     const truncated = text.slice(0, 8000); // safe token window
48:     const candidates = this.minerFn
49:       ? await this.mineWithModel("file_save", truncated)
50:       : this.mineModelFree(truncated);
51:     return candidates.map((content) =>
52:       this.store.add({
53:         content,
54:         type: "factual",
55:         layer: "working",
56:         tags: ["document", `file:${fileName}`],
57:         source: `document:${fileName}`,
58:       })
59:     );
60:   }
61: 
62:   // 4.3: no-model fallback. Concise direct summaries as short-term memories.
63:   mineModelFree(text: string): string[] {
64:     return text
65:       .split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+/)
66:       .map((s) => s.trim())
67:       .filter((s) => s.length >= 20 && s.length <= 300 && SIGNAL.test(s))
68:       .slice(0, 10);
69:   }
70: 
71:   private async mineWithModel(event: MiningEventType, text: string): Promise<string[]> {
72:     const prompt = `Extract durable memories from this ${event} as a strict JSON array of strings:\n\n${text}`;
73:     const rawResponse = await this.minerFn!(prompt);
74:     return parseStrictJsonArray(rawResponse);
75:   }
76: }
77: 
78: // Robust parsing: strip markdown fences, tolerate minor noise (section 4.1 step 3).
79: export function parseStrictJsonArray(raw: string): string[] {
80:   let cleaned = raw.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?\s*/i, "").replace(/```\s*$/, "").trim();
81:   const start = cleaned.indexOf("[");
82:   const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf("]");
83:   if (start !== -1 && end > start) cleaned = cleaned.slice(start, end + 1);
84:   try {
85:     const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);
86:     if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) return [];
87:     return parsed.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string" && x.trim().length >= 5);
88:   } catch {
89:     return [];
90:   }
91: }

1: // Conflict detection and resolution (AGENTS.md section 10). The losing record
2: // is marked supersededBy (kept, penalized in ranking), never deleted.
3: // Auto-resolve only at decision confidence >= 0.70; everything else queues.
4: 
5: import { DEFAULTS, clamp01 } from "./types.ts";
6: import type { ConflictRecord, MemoryRecord } from "./types.ts";
7: import { cosine } from "./embeddings.ts";
8: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
9: import { snapshot } from "./memoryStore.ts";
10: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
11: 
12: const OPPOSING_PAIRS: [RegExp, RegExp][] = [
13:   [/\balways\b/i, /\bnever\b/i],
14:   [/\benable[ds]?\b/i, /\bdisable[ds]?\b/i],
15:   [/\bprefer[s]?\b/i, /\bavoid[s]?|dislike[s]?\b/i],
16:   [/\bon\b/i, /\boff\b/i],
17:   [/\byes\b/i, /\bno\b/i],
18: ];
19: 
20: export class ConflictDetectionService {
21:   private conflicts: ConflictRecord[] = [];
22:   private seq = 0;
23: 
24:   constructor(
25:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
26:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
27:     private clock: () => number,
28:     private actor: string
29:   ) {}
30: 
31:   scan(): ConflictRecord[] {
32:     const found: ConflictRecord[] = [];
33:     const all = this.store.all();
34:     for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
35:       for (let j = i + 1; j < all.length; j++) {
36:         const conflict = this.check(all[i], all[j]);
37:         if (conflict) {
38:           found.push(conflict);
39:           this.conflicts.push(conflict);
40:           this.ledger.log(conflict.memoryA, "conflict_detected", this.actor, {
41:             details: { with: conflict.memoryB, reason: conflict.reason, confidence: conflict.confidence },
42:           });
43:         }
44:       }
45:     }
46:     return found;
47:   }
48: 
49:   private check(a: MemoryRecord, b: MemoryRecord): ConflictRecord | undefined {
50:     // supersedes relation suppresses conflict: it is an intended replacement.
51:     if (a.supersedes === b.id || b.supersedes === a.id || a.supersededBy === b.id || b.supersededBy === a.id) return undefined;
52: 
53:     const sim = cosine(a.embedding, b.embedding);
54:     let reason = "";
55:     let confidence = 0;
56: 
57:     for (const [p, q] of OPPOSING_PAIRS) {
58:       if ((p.test(a.content) && q.test(b.content)) || (q.test(a.content) && p.test(b.content))) {
59:         if (sim > 0.5) {
60:           reason = "opposing phrase pair on similar content";
61:           confidence = 0.5 + 0.3 * sim;
62:         }
63:       }
64:     }
65:     if (!reason && sim > 0.8) {
66:       const numsA = a.content.match(/\d+(\.\d+)?/g) ?? [];
67:       const numsB = b.content.match(/\d+(\.\d+)?/g) ?? [];
68:       if (numsA.length && numsB.length && numsA.join() !== numsB.join()) {
69:         reason = "high-similarity conflicting numeric values";
70:         confidence = 0.55 + 0.25 * sim;
71:       }
72:     }
73:     if (!reason) return undefined;
74: 
75:     // Confidence modifiers (section 10.1).
76:     const sharedEntities = a.entities.filter((e) => b.entities.includes(e));
77:     if (sharedEntities.length > 0) confidence += 0.1;
78:     if (a.domain === b.domain) confidence += 0.05;
79:     if (a.relatedTo.includes(b.id)) confidence -= 0.1; // explicit relation lowers false positives
80: 
81:     return {
82:       id: `conflict-${++this.seq}`,
83:       memoryA: a.id,
84:       memoryB: b.id,
85:       reason,
86:       confidence: clamp01(confidence),
87:       resolved: false,
88:     };
89:   }
90: 
91:   // Weighted auto-decision heuristics (section 10.2).
92:   autoResolve(conflict: ConflictRecord): "resolved" | "queued" {
93:     const a = this.store.get(conflict.memoryA)!;
94:     const b = this.store.get(conflict.memoryB)!;
95:     const scoreOf = (m: MemoryRecord) =>
96:       0.3 * (m.lastAccessed / Math.max(1, this.clock())) +
97:       0.2 * Math.min(1, m.accessCount / 10) +
98:       0.25 * m.confidence +
99:       0.1 * Math.min(1, m.content.length / 200) +
100:       0.15 * (m.provenance.origin === "user_correction" ? 1 : 0.5);
101:     const sa = scoreOf(a);
102:     const sb = scoreOf(b);
103:     const margin = Math.abs(sa - sb) / Math.max(sa, sb);
104:     const decisionConfidence = clamp01(conflict.confidence * 0.6 + margin * 0.8);
105: 
106:     if (decisionConfidence < DEFAULTS.conflictAutoResolveGate) return "queued";
107: 
108:     const winner = sa >= sb ? a : b;
109:     const loser = sa >= sb ? b : a;
110:     const prev = snapshot(loser);
111:     loser.supersededBy = winner.id; // kept and penalized, never deleted
112:     conflict.resolved = true;
113:     conflict.resolution = winner.id === conflict.memoryA ? "keep_a" : "keep_b";
114:     this.ledger.log(loser.id, "conflict_resolved", this.actor, {
115:       previousState: prev,
116:       newState: snapshot(loser),
117:       details: { conflictId: conflict.id, winner: winner.id, decisionConfidence: Number(decisionConfidence.toFixed(3)) },
118:     });
119:     this.store.persist();
120:     return "resolved";
121:   }
122: 
123:   queue(): ConflictRecord[] {
124:     return this.conflicts.filter((c) => !c.resolved);
125:   }
126: }

1: // Sleep cycle (AGENTS.md section 8). Preview-first: preview() computes the
2: // full action plan and mutates nothing; execute() takes a backup snapshot
3: // first and exposes restore(). Guardrails: superseding/current records,
4: // derived/synthesized memories, and relationship hubs are NEVER archived.
5: 
6: import { DAY_MS, DEFAULTS } from "./types.ts";
7: import type { MemoryRecord, SleepPreview, SleepReport } from "./types.ts";
8: import { cosine } from "./embeddings.ts";
9: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
10: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
11: 
12: const HUB_THRESHOLD = 3;
13: 
14: export class SleepCycleService {
15:   private backups = new Map<string, { records: MemoryRecord[]; seq: number }>();
16:   private backupSeq = 0;
17: 
18:   constructor(
19:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
20:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
21:     private clock: () => number,
22:     private actor: string
23:   ) {}
24: 
25:   preview(): SleepPreview {
26:     const now = this.clock();
27:     const all = this.store.all();
28:     const referenced = new Set<string>();
29:     for (const m of all) {
30:       for (const r of m.relatedTo) referenced.add(r);
31:       if (m.supersedes) referenced.add(m.supersedes);
32:       for (const d of m.derivedFrom ?? []) referenced.add(d);
33:     }
34: 
35:     const toConsolidate = all
36:       .filter((m) => m.layer === "short_term" && now - m.lastAccessed >= DEFAULTS.consolidationDays * DAY_MS)
37:       .map((m) => m.id);
38: 
39:     const toArchive = all
40:       .filter((m) => {
41:         const oldEnough = now - m.timestamp >= DEFAULTS.archiveMinDays * DAY_MS;
42:         const lowAccess = m.accessCount <= DEFAULTS.archiveMaxAccess;
43:         const unreferenced = !referenced.has(m.id);
44:         if (!(oldEnough && lowAccess && unreferenced)) return false;
45:         // Guardrails (section 8.2): never archive these three classes.
46:         if (m.supersedes) return false;                       // superseding/current record
47:         if ((m.derivedFrom ?? []).length > 0) return false;   // derived/synthesized memory
48:         if (m.relatedTo.length >= HUB_THRESHOLD) return false; // relationship hub
49:         return true;
50:       })
51:       .map((m) => m.id);
52: 
53:     const toSynthesize: string[][] = [];
54:     const used = new Set<string>();
55:     for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
56:       if (used.has(all[i].id)) continue;
57:       const group = [all[i]];
58:       for (let j = i + 1; j < all.length; j++) {
59:         if (used.has(all[j].id)) continue;
60:         if (cosine(all[i].embedding, all[j].embedding) >= DEFAULTS.synthesisCosine) group.push(all[j]);
61:       }
62:       if (group.length >= 2) {
63:         for (const g of group) used.add(g.id);
64:         toSynthesize.push(group.map((g) => g.id));
65:       }
66:     }
67: 
68:     return { toConsolidate, toArchive, toSynthesize };
69:   }
70: 
71:   execute(preview?: SleepPreview): SleepReport {
72:     const plan = preview ?? this.preview();
73:     const backupId = `backup-${++this.backupSeq}`;
74:     this.backups.set(backupId, this.store.snapshotAll());
75:     const actionLog: string[] = [`backup ${backupId} created`];
76: 
77:     for (const id of plan.toConsolidate) {
78:       const m = this.store.get(id);
79:       if (!m) continue;
80:       this.store.promote(id, "long_term");
81:       this.ledger.log(id, "sleep_consolidate", this.actor, { details: { from: "short_term", to: "long_term" } });
82:       actionLog.push(`consolidated ${id}`);
83:     }
84: 
85:     for (const id of plan.toArchive) {
86:       const m = this.store.get(id);
87:       if (!m) continue;
88:       this.ledger.log(id, "sleep_archive", this.actor, { details: { age: this.clock() - m.timestamp, accessCount: m.accessCount } });
89:       this.store.delete(id, "sleep archive");
90:       actionLog.push(`archived ${id}`);
91:     }
92: 
93:     let synthesized = 0;
94:     for (const group of plan.toSynthesize) {
95:       const members = group.map((id) => this.store.get(id)).filter((m): m is MemoryRecord => !!m);
96:       if (members.length < 2) continue;
97:       const merged = this.store.add({
98:         content: `Synthesis: ${members.map((m) => m.content).join(" | ")}`,
99:         type: "factual",
100:         layer: "long_term",
101:         tags: [...new Set(members.flatMap((m) => m.tags))],
102:         confidence: Math.max(...members.map((m) => m.confidence)),
103:         source: "sleep:synthesis",
104:         provenance: { origin: "sleep_synthesis", learnedAt: this.clock(), label: `synthesized from ${members.length} memories` },
105:         derivedFrom: members.map((m) => m.id),
106:       });
107:       this.ledger.log(merged.id, "sleep_synthesize", this.actor, { details: { sources: group } });
108:       for (const m of members) this.store.delete(m.id, "merged by sleep synthesis");
109:       synthesized++;
110:       actionLog.push(`synthesized ${merged.id} from ${group.join(", ")}`);
111:     }
112: 
113:     this.store.persist();
114:     return {
115:       backupId,
116:       consolidated: plan.toConsolidate.length,
117:       archived: plan.toArchive.length,
118:       synthesized,
119:       actionLog,
120:     };
121:   }
122: 
123:   restore(backupId: string): void {
124:     const backup = this.backups.get(backupId);
125:     if (!backup) throw new Error(`H-MEM: unknown backup ${backupId}`);
126:     this.store.restoreAll(backup.records, backup.seq);
127:     this.ledger.log("*", "restore", this.actor, { details: { backupId } });
128:   }
129: }

1: // Dreaming (AGENTS.md section 7): constructive synthesis with a human
2: // approval boundary. Proposals are NEVER auto-materialized; only approve()
3: // turns one into durable memory, with derivedFrom lineage.
4: 
5: import { DEFAULTS } from "./types.ts";
6: import type { DreamProposal, MemoryRecord } from "./types.ts";
7: import { cosine, jaccard } from "./embeddings.ts";
8: import type { MemoryStoreService } from "./memoryStore.ts";
9: import type { TrustLedgerService } from "./trustLedger.ts";
10: 
11: export class DreamingService {
12:   private proposals = new Map<string, DreamProposal>();
13:   private seq = 0;
14: 
15:   constructor(
16:     private store: MemoryStoreService,
17:     private ledger: TrustLedgerService,
18:     private clock: () => number,
19:     private actor: string
20:   ) {}
21: 
22:   // Multi-signal relatedness: content similarity, tag overlap, shared domain/type, entity overlap.
23:   private relatedness(a: MemoryRecord, b: MemoryRecord): number {
24:     return (
25:       0.5 * Math.max(0, cosine(a.embedding, b.embedding)) +
26:       0.2 * jaccard(a.tags, b.tags) +
27:       0.1 * (a.domain === b.domain ? 1 : 0) +
28:       0.2 * jaccard(a.entities, b.entities)
29:     );
30:   }
31: 
32:   private cluster(): MemoryRecord[][] {
33:     const all = this.store.all();
34:     const used = new Set<string>();
35:     const clusters: MemoryRecord[][] = [];
36:     for (const seed of all) {
37:       if (used.has(seed.id)) continue;
38:       const group = [seed];
39:       for (const other of all) {
40:         if (other.id === seed.id || used.has(other.id)) continue;
41:         if (this.relatedness(seed, other) >= DEFAULTS.dreamRelatedness) group.push(other);
42:       }
43:       if (group.length >= DEFAULTS.dreamClusterMinSize) {
44:         for (const g of group) used.add(g.id);
45:         clusters.push(group);
46:       }
47:     }
48:     return clusters;
49:   }
50: 
51:   dream(): DreamProposal[] {
52:     const created: DreamProposal[] = [];
53:     const propose = (p: Omit<DreamProposal, "id" | "status">): void => {
54:       const proposal: DreamProposal = { ...p, id: `dream-${++this.seq}`, status: "proposed" };
55:       this.proposals.set(proposal.id, proposal);
56:       created.push(proposal);
57:       this.ledger.log(proposal.id, "dream_proposed", this.actor, { details: { type: p.type, derivedFrom: p.derivedFrom } });
58:     };
59: 
60:     // Insights from clusters.
61:     let insights = 0;
62:     for (const cluster of this.cluster()) {
63:       if (insights >= DEFAULTS.maxDreamProposalsPerType) break;
64:       const domains = [...new Set(cluster.map((m) => m.domain))].join("/");
65:       propose({
66:         type: "insight",
67:         content: `Across ${cluster.length} related memories (${domains}): ${cluster.map((m) => m.content).join(" + ")}`,
68:         derivedFrom: cluster.map((m) => m.id),
69:       });
70:       insights++;
71:     }
72: 
73:     // Domain suggestions for uncategorized memories.
74:     let domains = 0;
75:     for (const m of this.store.all()) {
76:       if (domains >= DEFAULTS.maxDreamProposalsPerType) break;
77:       if (m.domain !== "general") continue;
78:       const suggested = this.store.classifyDomain(m.content, m.tags, m.type);
79:       if (suggested !== "general") {
80:         propose({ type: "domain", content: `Reclassify "${m.content.slice(0, 60)}" as ${suggested}`, derivedFrom: [m.id], suggestedDomain: suggested });
81:         domains++;
82:       }
83:     }
84: 
85:     // Invariants from preference/personal/correction signals.
86:     let invariants = 0;
87:     const prefs = this.store.all().filter((m) => m.type === "preference" || m.type === "personal" || m.tags.includes("event:user_correction"));
88:     const byDomain = new Map<string, MemoryRecord[]>();
89:     for (const p of prefs) {
90:       const list = byDomain.get(p.domain) ?? [];
91:       list.push(p);
92:       byDomain.set(p.domain, list);
93:     }
94:     for (const [domain, list] of byDomain) {
95:       if (invariants >= DEFAULTS.maxDreamProposalsPerType) break;
96:       if (list.length < 2) continue;
97:       propose({
98:         type: "invariant",
99:         content: `Stable pattern in ${domain}: ${list.map((m) => m.content).join("; ")}`,
100:         derivedFrom: list.map((m) => m.id),
101:       });
102:       invariants++;
103:     }
104: 
105:     return created;
106:   }
107: 
108:   pending(): DreamProposal[] {
109:     return [...this.proposals.values()].filter((p) => p.status === "proposed");
110:   }
111: 
112:   approve(proposalId: string): MemoryRecord | undefined {
113:     const p = this.proposals.get(proposalId);
114:     if (!p || p.status !== "proposed") throw new Error(`H-MEM: no pending proposal ${proposalId}`);
115:     p.status = "approved";
116:     this.ledger.log(proposalId, "dream_approved", this.actor, { details: { type: p.type } });
117: 
118:     if (p.type === "domain") {
119:       for (const id of p.derivedFrom) {
120:         const m = this.store.get(id);
121:         if (m && p.suggestedDomain) this.store.update(id, { domain: p.suggestedDomain });
122:       }
123:       return undefined;
124:     }
125:     // insight -> long-term factual; invariant -> long-term preference. Both carry lineage.
126:     return this.store.add({
127:       content: p.content,
128:       type: p.type === "insight" ? "factual" : "preference",
129:       layer: "long_term",
130:       tags: [`dream:${p.type}`],
131:       confidence: 0.75,
132:       source: "dreaming",
133:       provenance: { origin: "dream", learnedAt: this.clock(), label: `approved ${p.type} proposal` },
134:       derivedFrom: p.derivedFrom,
135:     });
136:   }
137: 
138:   reject(proposalId: string): void {
139:     const p = this.proposals.get(proposalId);
140:     if (!p || p.status !== "proposed") throw new Error(`H-MEM: no pending proposal ${proposalId}`);
141:     p.status = "rejected"; // logged, not materialized
142:     this.ledger.log(proposalId, "dream_rejected", this.actor, { details: { type: p.type } });
143:   }
144: }

1: /**
2:  * Stable, deterministic, content-addressable IDs (docs/stable-ids.md).
3:  *
4:  * Same input, same ID, on every machine, every re-run, every backfill.
5:  * This module has zero dependencies: sha-256 is implemented inline so the
6:  * same code runs in Node and in the browser bundle.
7:  */
8: 
9: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
10: /* sha-256 (pure TypeScript, synchronous)                              */
11: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
12: 
13: const K = new Uint32Array([
14:   0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
15:   0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
16:   0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
17:   0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
18:   0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
19:   0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
20:   0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
21:   0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,
22: ]);
23: 
24: function rotr(x: number, n: number): number {
25:   return (x >>> n) | (x << (32 - n));
26: }
27: 
28: /** Hex-encoded sha-256 of a UTF-8 string. */
29: export function sha256Hex(input: string): string {
30:   const data = new TextEncoder().encode(input);
31:   const len = data.length;
32:   const bitLenHi = Math.floor((len / 0x20000000)) >>> 0;
33:   const bitLenLo = (len << 3) >>> 0;
34: 
35:   const paddedLen = (((len + 8) >> 6) + 1) << 6;
36:   const padded = new Uint8Array(paddedLen);
37:   padded.set(data);
38:   padded[len] = 0x80;
39:   const dv = new DataView(padded.buffer);
40:   dv.setUint32(paddedLen - 8, bitLenHi);
41:   dv.setUint32(paddedLen - 4, bitLenLo);
42: 
43:   let h0 = 0x6a09e667, h1 = 0xbb67ae85, h2 = 0x3c6ef372, h3 = 0xa54ff53a;
44:   let h4 = 0x510e527f, h5 = 0x9b05688c, h6 = 0x1f83d9ab, h7 = 0x5be0cd19;
45: 
46:   const w = new Uint32Array(64);
47:   for (let i = 0; i < paddedLen; i += 64) {
48:     for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) w[t] = dv.getUint32(i + t * 4);
49:     for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
50:       const s0 = rotr(w[t - 15], 7) ^ rotr(w[t - 15], 18) ^ (w[t - 15] >>> 3);
51:       const s1 = rotr(w[t - 2], 17) ^ rotr(w[t - 2], 19) ^ (w[t - 2] >>> 10);
52:       w[t] = (w[t - 16] + s0 + w[t - 7] + s1) >>> 0;
53:     }
54:     let a = h0, b = h1, c = h2, d = h3, e = h4, f = h5, g = h6, h = h7;
55:     for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
56:       const S1 = rotr(e, 6) ^ rotr(e, 11) ^ rotr(e, 25);
57:       const ch = (e & f) ^ (~e & g);
58:       const temp1 = (h + S1 + ch + K[t] + w[t]) >>> 0;
59:       const S0 = rotr(a, 2) ^ rotr(a, 13) ^ rotr(a, 22);
60:       const maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
61:       const temp2 = (S0 + maj) >>> 0;
62:       h = g; g = f; f = e;
63:       e = (d + temp1) >>> 0;
64:       d = c; c = b; b = a;
65:       a = (temp1 + temp2) >>> 0;
66:     }
67:     h0 = (h0 + a) >>> 0; h1 = (h1 + b) >>> 0; h2 = (h2 + c) >>> 0; h3 = (h3 + d) >>> 0;
68:     h4 = (h4 + e) >>> 0; h5 = (h5 + f) >>> 0; h6 = (h6 + g) >>> 0; h7 = (h7 + h) >>> 0;
69:   }
70: 
71:   return [h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]
72:     .map((x) => x.toString(16).padStart(8, "0"))
73:     .join("");
74: }
75: 
76: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
77: /* Canonical JSON                                                      */
78: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
79: 
80: /**
81:  * Deterministic JSON serialization: object keys sorted, undefined members
82:  * dropped. JSON key order in JS is insertion order, so a naive
83:  * JSON.stringify comparison gives false negatives; the idempotency diff
84:  * (scripts/idempotency-check.ts) depends on this function instead.
85:  */
86: export function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string {
87:   if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") {
88:     const s = JSON.stringify(value);
89:     return s === undefined ? "null" : s;
90:   }
91:   if (Array.isArray(value)) {
92:     return "[" + value.map((v) => canonicalJson(v)).join(",") + "]";
93:   }
94:   const obj = value as Record<string, unknown>;
95:   const keys = Object.keys(obj)
96:     .filter((k) => obj[k] !== undefined)
97:     .sort();
98:   return "{" + keys.map((k) => JSON.stringify(k) + ":" + canonicalJson(obj[k])).join(",") + "}";
99: }
100: 
101: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
102: /* Name normalization                                                  */
103: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
104: 
105: /**
106:  * normalizeName per docs/stable-ids.md:
107:  *   NFKD normalize -> strip combining marks -> lowercase -> collapse whitespace -> trim
108:  *
109:  * Notes on the edge cases this must catch (dedupe correctness depends on it):
110:  * - Diacritics: "Jose Garcia" and the accented spelling must normalize identically
111:  *   (NFKD decomposes the accents into combining marks, which are then stripped).
112:  * - Non-breaking space (U+00A0): NFKD decomposes it to a regular space; the
113:  *   whitespace collapse then folds runs of any whitespace into one space.
114:  * - Zero-width characters (U+200B..U+200D, U+FEFF) carry no name content and are
115:  *   stripped explicitly, since NFKD leaves them alone.
116:  * - Over-normalization is the opposite failure: "Acme Corp" and
117:  *   "Acme Corporation" are DIFFERENT names and must produce DIFFERENT ids.
118:  *   Normalization never abbreviates, stems, or drops word characters.
119:  */
120: export function normalizeName(name: string): string {
121:   return name
122:     .normalize("NFKD")
123:     .replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, "") // strip combining marks
124:     .replace(/[​-‍﻿]/g, "") // strip zero-width chars
125:     .toLowerCase()
126:     .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
127:     .trim();
128: }
129: 
130: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
131: /* ID derivation                                                       */
132: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
133: 
134: /** Externally keyed entity or context: the literal grammar `type:system:externalId`. */
135: export function externalId(type: string, system: string, id: string): string {
136:   return `${type}:${system}:${id}`;
137: }
138: 
139: /** Name-keyed entity: ent_<first 16 hex of sha256(`${type}:${normalizeName(name)}`)>. */
140: export function entityIdFromName(type: string, name: string): string {
141:   return `ent_${sha256Hex(`${type}:${normalizeName(name)}`).slice(0, 16)}`;
142: }
143: 
144: /**
145:  * Context id.
146:  *
147:  * Ruling: docs/stable-ids.md derives context ids as hash(type + canonicalKey +
148:  * parent), but every shipped example references externally keyed contexts by
149:  * the literal `type:system:externalId` grammar (e.g. "season:gridiron:145").
150:  * So: externally keyed contexts use the literal grammar (the caller's external
151:  * id is already unique within its system, parent included by construction);
152:  * attr-keyed contexts (no external key) are hashed WITH the parent, which is
153:  * what makes week:14 under season:145 a different id than under season:144.
154:  */
155: export function contextIdFromAttrs(
156:   type: string,
157:   attrs: Record<string, unknown>,
158:   parent?: string,
159: ): string {
160:   return `ctx_${sha256Hex(`${type}:${canonicalJson(attrs)}:${parent ?? ""}`).slice(0, 16)}`;
161: }
162: 
163: /** Relationship id: hash(from + type + to + context? + validFrom?). Re-adding the same edge is a no-op. */
164: export function relationshipId(
165:   from: string,
166:   type: string,
167:   to: string,
168:   context?: string,
169:   validFrom?: string,
170: ): string {
171:   return `rel_${sha256Hex(`${from}|${type}|${to}|${context ?? ""}|${validFrom ?? ""}`).slice(0, 16)}`;
172: }
173: 
174: /** Fact id: content-addressed dedupe key. Asserting the identical fact twice is a no-op. */
175: export function factId(
176:   about: string,
177:   predicate: string,
178:   value: unknown,
179:   assertedAt: string,
180:   sourceKind: string,
181:   sourceUrl?: string,
182: ): string {
183:   return `fact_${sha256Hex(
184:     `${about}|${predicate}|${canonicalJson(value)}|${assertedAt}|${sourceKind}|${sourceUrl ?? ""}`,
185:   ).slice(0, 16)}`;
186: }

1: // Entity resolution (AGENTS.md section on merge detection). Banded thresholds:
2: //
3: //   similarity >= 0.85            -> auto-merge   (0.85 EXACTLY is auto-merge)
4: //   0.82 <= similarity < 0.85     -> operator review queue (0.82 EXACTLY queues)
5: //   similarity < 0.82             -> new entity
6: //
7: // Similarity is Levenshtein-based: 1 - distance / max(lenA, lenB), computed on
8: // NORMALIZED names (stableIds.normalizeName). The spec names the bands but not
9: // the normalization input; this reference pins it to normalized names so that
10: // diacritics and whitespace never inflate distance.
11: 
12: import { normalizeName } from "./stableIds.ts";
13: 
14: export function levenshtein(a: string, b: string): number {
15:   if (a === b) return 0;
16:   const m = a.length;
17:   const n = b.length;
18:   if (m === 0) return n;
19:   if (n === 0) return m;
20:   let prev = new Array<number>(n + 1);
21:   let curr = new Array<number>(n + 1);
22:   for (let j = 0; j <= n; j++) prev[j] = j;
23:   for (let i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
24:     curr[0] = i;
25:     for (let j = 1; j <= n; j++) {
26:       const cost = a[i - 1] === b[j - 1] ? 0 : 1;
27:       curr[j] = Math.min(prev[j] + 1, curr[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + cost);
28:     }
29:     [prev, curr] = [curr, prev];
30:   }
31:   return prev[n];
32: }
33: 
34: export function nameSimilarity(rawA: string, rawB: string): number {
35:   const a = normalizeName(rawA);
36:   const b = normalizeName(rawB);
37:   if (a.length === 0 && b.length === 0) return 1;
38:   const maxLen = Math.max(a.length, b.length);
39:   if (maxLen === 0) return 1;
40:   return 1 - levenshtein(a, b) / maxLen;
41: }
42: 
43: export type ResolutionDecision = "auto-merge" | "review" | "new";
44: 
45: export function decide(similarity: number, autoMergeAt = 0.85, reviewLower = 0.82): ResolutionDecision {
46:   if (similarity >= autoMergeAt) return "auto-merge"; // boundary value merges
47:   if (similarity >= reviewLower) return "review";     // boundary value queues
48:   return "new";
49: }
50: 
51: // Clustering gate for the ingest pipeline: entity-overlap Jaccard >= 0.5
52: // co-clusters two observations.
53: export function jaccard(a: Iterable<string>, b: Iterable<string>): number {
54:   const sa = new Set(a);
55:   const sb = new Set(b);
56:   if (sa.size === 0 || sb.size === 0) return 0;
57:   let inter = 0;
58:   for (const x of sa) if (sb.has(x)) inter++;
59:   return inter / (sa.size + sb.size - inter);
60: }

1: // Event-sourced canonical store. State is a fold over an append-only event
2: // log; views are projections of the fold. Persistence is a JSON file per
3: // namespace (.world/<namespace>.json) replayed on load. Every mutation writes
4: // an audit entry; the control plane reads the audit log.
5: 
6: import fs from "node:fs";
7: import path from "node:path";
8: import type {
9:   AuditEntry, Context, Entity, EventKind, Fact, Relationship, Snapshot, StoredProvenance,
10:   WorldEvent, MergeProposal, ObservationRecord, StoryAggregate, ScoreSnapshot,
11: } from "./types.ts";
12: 
13: export interface FoldedState {
14:   entities: Map<string, Entity>;
15:   contexts: Map<string, Context>;
16:   relationships: Map<string, Relationship>;
17:   facts: Map<string, Fact>;
18:   aliases: Map<string, string>; // aliasId -> primaryId
19: }
20: 
21: export class EventStore {
22:   events: WorldEvent[] = [];
23:   audit: AuditEntry[] = [];
24:   observations = new Map<string, ObservationRecord>();
25:   stories = new Map<string, StoryAggregate>();
26:   scores: ScoreSnapshot[] = [];
27:   mergeQueue: MergeProposal[] = [];
28:   state: FoldedState = {
29:     entities: new Map(),
30:     contexts: new Map(),
31:     relationships: new Map(),
32:     facts: new Map(),
33:     aliases: new Map(),
34:   };
35:   private seq = 0;
36:   private auditSeq = 0;
37:   private file?: string;
38:   private subscribers = new Set<(e: WorldEvent) => void>();
39: 
40:   constructor(namespace: string, storage: "memory" | "local", directory?: string) {
41:     if (storage === "local") {
42:       const dir = path.join(directory ?? process.cwd(), ".world");
43:       fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
44:       this.file = path.join(dir, `${namespace}.json`);
45:       if (fs.existsSync(this.file)) {
46:         const saved = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(this.file, "utf-8")) as {
47:           events: WorldEvent[];
48:           audit: AuditEntry[];
49:           observations: [string, ObservationRecord][];
50:           stories: [string, StoryAggregate][];
51:           scores: ScoreSnapshot[];
52:           mergeQueue: MergeProposal[];
53:         };
54:         this.audit = saved.audit ?? [];
55:         this.auditSeq = this.audit.length ? this.audit[this.audit.length - 1].seq : 0;
56:         this.observations = new Map(saved.observations ?? []);
57:         this.stories = new Map(saved.stories ?? []);
58:         this.scores = saved.scores ?? [];
59:         this.mergeQueue = saved.mergeQueue ?? [];
60:         for (const e of saved.events ?? []) this.applyAndRecord(e, false);
61:       }
62:     }
63:   }
64: 
65:   append(kind: EventKind, payload: WorldEvent["payload"], at: string): WorldEvent {
66:     const event: WorldEvent = { id: `evt_${this.seq + 1}`, seq: this.seq + 1, kind, payload, schemaVersion: 1, at };
67:     this.applyAndRecord(event, true);
68:     return event;
69:   }
70: 
71:   private applyAndRecord(event: WorldEvent, isNew: boolean): void {
72:     this.seq = Math.max(this.seq, event.seq);
73:     if (isNew) this.events.push(event);
74:     else this.events.push(event);
75:     this.fold(event);
76:     if (isNew) {
77:       this.persist();
78:       for (const fn of this.subscribers) fn(event);
79:     }
80:   }
81: 
82:   private fold(event: WorldEvent): void {
83:     switch (event.kind) {
84:       case "upsertEntity": {

1: // The canonical 10-step ingest pipeline (AGENTS.md section 4.1). Each step is
2: // a named function so the pipeline reads like the spec. Idempotency contract:
3: // re-running the same batch produces the same world state and an empty diff.
4: // Every derived timestamp comes from the OBSERVATION, never the wall clock.
5: 
6: import { canonicalJson, entityIdFromName, sha256Hex } from "./stableIds.ts";
7: import { jaccard } from "./resolve.ts";
8: import type { EventStore } from "./store.ts";
9: import type { IngestObservation, IngestReport, ObservationRecord, ScoreSnapshot, StoryAggregate } from "./types.ts";
10: 
11: const CLUSTER_JACCARD = 0.5;
12: const HOUR_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
13: 
14: export function runIngestPipeline(
15:   store: EventStore,
16:   observations: IngestObservation[],
17:   upsert: (obs: IngestObservation) => { entityId: string; entityIds: string[] },
18:   timer: () => number
19: ): IngestReport {
20:   const runId = `run_${sha256Hex(canonicalJson(observations.map((o) => o.externalId))).slice(0, 12)}`;
21:   const timings: IngestReport["stepTimingsMs"] = [];
22:   const before = canonicalJson(worldStateShape(store));
23:   let eventsBefore = store.events.length;
24: 
25:   const time = <T>(step: number, name: string, fn: () => T): T => {
26:     const t0 = timer();
27:     const out = fn();
28:     timings.push({ step, name, ms: timer() - t0 });
29:     return out;
30:   };
31: 
32:   // 1. Reconcile stale edges/aggregates: recompute staleness from observation times.
33:   time(1, "reconcile-stale", () => {
34:     const latest = observations.reduce((max, o) => (o.at > max ? o.at : max), "");
35:     for (const rec of store.observations.values()) {
36:       rec.stale = latest !== "" && rec.at < isoDaysBefore(latest, 30);
37:     }
38:   });
39: 
40:   // 2. Cluster/classify raw items (entity-overlap Jaccard >= 0.5 co-clusters).
41:   const fresh: { obs: IngestObservation; checksum: string }[] = [];
42:   const skipped: IngestObservation[] = [];
43:   time(2, "cluster-classify", () => {
44:     for (const obs of observations) {
45:       const checksum = sha256Hex(canonicalJson({ externalId: obs.externalId, title: obs.title, text: obs.text ?? "", at: obs.at }));
46:       const existing = store.observations.get(obs.externalId);
47:       if (existing && existing.checksum === checksum) skipped.push(obs);
48:       else fresh.push({ obs, checksum });
49:     }
50:   });
51: 
52:   // 3. Persist primary aggregates: upsert observation entities + mentioned entities.
53:   const records: ObservationRecord[] = [];
54:   time(3, "persist-aggregates", () => {
55:     for (const { obs, checksum } of fresh) {
56:       const { entityId, entityIds } = upsert(obs);
57:       const record: ObservationRecord = {
58:         id: `obs_${sha256Hex(obs.externalId).slice(0, 12)}`,
59:         externalId: obs.externalId,
60:         entityId,
61:         checksum,
62:         at: obs.at,
63:         entityIds,
64:         stale: false,
65:       };
66:       store.observations.set(obs.externalId, record);
67:       records.push(record);
68:     }
69:   });
70: 
71:   // Group fresh + existing observations into stories by entity overlap.
72:   const clusters: ObservationRecord[][] = [];
73:   time(2, "story-grouping", () => {
74:     const all = [...store.observations.values()].sort((a, b) => a.externalId.localeCompare(b.externalId));
75:     const used = new Set<string>();
76:     for (const seed of all) {
77:       if (used.has(seed.externalId)) continue;
78:       const group = [seed];
79:       used.add(seed.externalId);
80:       for (const other of all) {
81:         if (used.has(other.externalId)) continue;
82:         if (jaccard(seed.entityIds ?? [], other.entityIds ?? []) >= CLUSTER_JACCARD) {
83:           group.push(other);
84:           used.add(other.externalId);
85:         }
86:       }
87:       clusters.push(group);
88:     }
89:   });
90: 
91:   // 4. Score/measure: velocity = mentions per hour over BUCKETED windows.
92:   // 5. Infer derived records (milestones). 6. Persist edges is handled by the
93:   // upsert callback (mentions edges). 7. Rebuild materialized views happens on
94:   // read in this reference (views project the fold). 8. Patch source items.
95:   // 9. Rebuild aggregates. 10. Mark stale items.
96:   time(4, "score-measure", () => {
97:     for (const group of clusters) {
98:       const memberIds = group.map((g) => g.externalId).sort();
99:       const storyId = `story_${sha256Hex(canonicalJson(memberIds)).slice(0, 12)}`;
100:       const times = group.map((g) => Date.parse(g.at)).sort((a, b) => a - b);
101:       const lastAt = times[times.length - 1];
102:       const velocity = (windowMs: number) => {
103:         // Bucketed rate: mentions inside the window ending at the newest
104:         // observation, divided by the window's hours. A naive
105:         // mentions/total-hours calculation fails trend detection.
106:         const inWindow = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - windowMs).length;
107:         return inWindow / (windowMs / HOUR_MS);
108:       };
109:       const prevHour = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - 2 * HOUR_MS && t <= lastAt - HOUR_MS).length;
110:       const currHour = times.filter((t) => t > lastAt - HOUR_MS).length;
111:       const score: ScoreSnapshot = {
112:         storyId,
113:         at: new Date(lastAt).toISOString(),
114:         velocity1h: velocity(HOUR_MS),
115:         velocity24h: velocity(24 * HOUR_MS),
116:         velocity7d: velocity(7 * 24 * HOUR_MS),
117:         trendDirection: Math.sign(currHour - prevHour) as -1 | 0 | 1,
118:       };
119:       store.scores = store.scores.filter((s) => s.storyId !== storyId);
120:       store.scores.push(score);
121: 
122:       const entityIds = [...new Set(group.flatMap((g) => g.entityIds ?? []))].sort();
123:       const story: StoryAggregate = {
124:         id: storyId,
125:         title: group[0].externalId,
126:         memberIds,
127:         entityNames: entityIds.map((id) => id),
128:         entityIds,
129:         sources: [],
130:         firstAt: new Date(times[0]).toISOString(),
131:         lastAt: new Date(lastAt).toISOString(),
132:         milestones: group.length >= 2 ? [{ kind: "multi-source", at: new Date(times[1]).toISOString() }] : [],
133:       };
134:       store.stories.set(storyId, story);
135:       for (const rec of group) rec.storyId = storyId; // step 8: patch source items
136:     }
137:   });
138: 
139:   time(9, "rebuild-aggregates", () => {
140:     for (const entity of store.state.entities.values()) {
141:       const mentions = [...store.observations.values()].filter((o) => o.entityIds?.includes(entity.id));
142:       if (mentions.length === 0) continue;
143:       const times = mentions.map((m) => m.at).sort();
144:       entity.aggregates = {
145:         mentionCount: mentions.length,
146:         firstSeenAt: times[0],
147:         lastSeenAt: times[times.length - 1],
148:         linkedStoryIds: [...new Set(mentions.map((m) => m.storyId).filter((s): s is string => !!s))].sort(),
149:       };
150:     }
151:   });
152: 
153:   store.persist();
154:   const after = canonicalJson(worldStateShape(store));
155:   const report: IngestReport = {
156:     runId,
157:     processed: fresh.length,
158:     skippedUnchanged: skipped.length,
159:     clusters: clusters.length,
160:     eventsAppended: store.events.length - eventsBefore,
161:     changed: before !== after,
162:     stepTimingsMs: timings,
163:   };
164:   store.logAudit("ingest", "pipeline", `run ${runId}: ${fresh.length} processed, ${skipped.length} skipped`, undefined, runId, observations[0]?.at);
165:   return report;
166: }
167: 
168: // The idempotency diff surface: everything derived from observations, in
169: // canonical (sorted-key, sorted-collection) form.
170: export function worldStateShape(store: EventStore): unknown {
171:   return {
172:     entities: [...store.state.entities.values()].sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
173:     contexts: [...store.state.contexts.values()].sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
174:     relationships: [...store.state.relationships.values()].sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
175:     facts: [...store.state.facts.values()].sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
176:     observations: [...store.observations.values()].sort((a, b) => a.externalId.localeCompare(b.externalId)),
177:     stories: [...store.stories.values()].sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
178:   };
179: }
180: 
181: function isoDaysBefore(iso: string, days: number): string {
182:   return new Date(Date.parse(iso) - days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
183: }

import type { IntentRegistry } from './types';

// The registry is the entire action surface for this app. Scout cannot route
// an intent that is not listed here.
export const APP_INTENT_REGISTRY: IntentRegistry = {
  version: 1,
  intents: [
    {
      id: 'GENERAL',
      category: 'general',
      description: 'Safe conversational fallback. Never routes to tools and never guesses a high-risk intent.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
      capabilities: [],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['hello', 'what can you help me with?', "what's the weather tomorrow?"],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.add',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Add a new task to the local list.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { title: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['title'],
      },
      capabilities: ['task.write'],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Add a task', 'Create a task', 'Remind me to buy milk', 'New task: call mom'],
      triggers: ['^(add|create|new)\\b', 'remind me to'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.complete',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Mark a task as complete.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { task: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['task'],
      },
      capabilities: ['task.write'],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Complete buy milk', 'Finish the report', 'Mark buy milk as done', 'Check off buy milk'],
      triggers: ['^(complete|finish|done|check off|mark)\\b'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.uncomplete',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Reopen a completed task.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { task: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['task'],
      },
      capabilities: ['task.write'],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Reopen buy milk', 'Mark buy milk as active', 'Uncomplete the report'],
      triggers: ['^(reopen|uncomplete|uncheck)\\b', 'mark .* active'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.delete',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Delete one task or clear a scope of tasks.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { task: { type: 'string' }, scope: { type: 'string', enum: ['all', 'completed'] } },
      },
      capabilities: ['task.write'],
      riskClass: 'high',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Delete buy milk', 'Remove the report', 'Clear completed tasks', 'Delete all tasks'],
      triggers: ['^(delete|remove|clear|wipe)\\b'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.rename',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Rename an existing task.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: { task: { type: 'string' }, title: { type: 'string' } },
        required: ['task', 'title'],
      },
      capabilities: ['task.write'],
      riskClass: 'medium',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Rename buy milk to get milk', 'Edit the report title', 'Change buy milk to get milk'],
      triggers: ['^(rename|edit|change)\\b'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.list',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Show the task list.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
      capabilities: [],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Show my tasks', 'List all tasks', 'What are my tasks?'],
      triggers: ['^(?:show|list|display)\\s+(?:me\\s+)?(?:all\\s+)?(?:my\\s+)?tasks?$', 'what are my tasks'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.filter',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Change the visible task filter to active, completed, or all.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { filter: { type: 'string', enum: ['active', 'completed', 'all'] } } },
      capabilities: [],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['Show active tasks', 'Show completed tasks', 'Filter by active'],
      triggers: ['show (?:me )?(?:the )?(active|completed)\\b', 'filter (?:by )?(active|completed|all)'],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.summary',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Summarize progress and remaining task counts.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
      capabilities: [],
      riskClass: 'low',
      surfaces: ['chat'],
      roles: ['*'],
      examples: ['How many tasks are left?', 'Summarize my tasks', "What's my progress?"],
      triggers: ['how many tasks', 'summarize my tasks', 'task progress', "what's left"],
      version: 1,
    },
    {
      id: 'task.plan',
      category: 'task',
      description: 'Turn a goal into a long-horizon plan with Markovian.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { goal: { type: 'string' } } },
      capabilities: ['markovian.chain'],
      riskClass: 'low',

# Angular To-Do App

A small, responsive to-do list built with Angular 22, standalone components, signals, and `localStorage`. No backend, no auth, no extra UI libraries.

## Features

- Add, edit, complete, and delete tasks
- Filter by All, Active, and Completed with live counts
- Remaining-task counter
- Tasks persist across refreshes via `localStorage`
- Empty state for each filter
- Keyboard-friendly editing (`Enter` saves, `Escape` cancels, double-click a title to edit)
- Mobile-responsive layout with a minimal, modern UI

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

Open `http://localhost:4200`.

## Verify it

```bash
npm test        # Vitest unit tests
npm run build   # production build
```

## Structure

```text
src/app/
  models/task.model.ts                  Task and filter types
  services/task-store.ts                Signal store, derived views, localStorage
  directives/autofocus.ts               Focus helper for inline editing
  components/task-input/                Add-task form
  components/task-filters/              All / Active / Completed control
  components/task-item/                 One task row with edit and delete
  app.ts / app.html / app.css           Page shell and empty state
```

`TaskStore` is the only place that mutates tasks. Components are presentational and emit events; derived values (`visibleTasks`, `remainingCount`, `counts`) are `computed` signals, so the UI stays consistent automatically.

## Meterless fit review

See [docs/meterless-fit.md](docs/meterless-fit.md) for where H-MEM, World Model, Markovian, and Scout Intent would plug into this app, what each would improve, and what is deliberately not adopted.

--- fit doc ---
# Meterless Fit Review

This document maps the four Meterless engines onto this Angular to-do app. It is intentionally honest about what is useful now, what is useful only after a specific feature exists, and what would be over-engineering today.

## What the Meterless engines actually are

All four are **implementation specs**, not runtime libraries:

- `H-MEM`, `World Model`, and `Markovian` ship an `AGENTS.md`, deep-dive docs, examples, and a reference implementation. There is no installable npm package. You build the engine in your stack.
- `Scout Intent` ships a spec plus a real eval harness that scores your implementation through `SCOUT_IMPL`.

That matters for a small local app: adopting an engine means building and maintaining a subsystem, not adding a dependency.

## This app's architecture in one paragraph

`TaskStore` (`src/app/services/task-store.ts`) is the single source of truth. It holds a `Task[]` signal, derives `visibleTasks`, `remainingCount`, `completedCount`, and `counts` with `computed`, and mirrors the list to `localStorage` through an `effect`. Components are standalone, `OnPush`, and presentational: they emit events and never mutate state directly. There is no backend, no model call, and no multi-user concurrency.

## Where each engine would plug in

| Engine           | Natural seam in this codebase                                                                                                                                                | What it would improve for users                                                                                                                                                                                             | What it costs                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **H-MEM**        | A new `src/app/ai/memory/` service, injected only into an assistant feature. `TaskStore` stays the system of record for tasks.                                               | An assistant that remembers preferences and corrections across sessions: "don't schedule chores before 9am", "I always shop on Saturday", "the last plan was too granular". Retrieval can explain why it surfaced a memory. | Embeddings, a persistence tier (IndexedDB), a mining pipeline, and an LLM. H-MEM's dreaming, sleep cycle, conflict detection, and trust ledger are large subsystems.            |
| **World Model**  | The persistence boundary inside `TaskStore`. Replace the `Task[]` snapshot with an append-only `TaskEvent[]` plus a projector. Add `task-events.ts` and `task-projector.ts`. | Undo/redo, an audit trail, safe multi-tab or multi-device merge, conflict resolution, and provenance ("who changed this and when").                                                                                         | Event schema design, projections, migration, compaction, and eventual-consistency handling. The operator control plane and enrichment workers are unnecessary for one user.     |
| **Markovian**    | A new `src/app/ai/planning/` service used only for long AI jobs, such as "break this goal into 30 subtasks" or an agent that edits many tasks over several steps.            | Long AI planning stays inside the model's context window, with flat per-step cost, checkpoints, progress, and resume. Short requests are unaffected.                                                                        | An LLM provider, a generator function, run-state persistence, and a chunk configuration. For normal add/toggle/edit/delete there is nothing to compress.                        |
| **Scout Intent** | A new `src/app/ai/scout/` layer in front of any AI or tool action. Registry entries such as `task.add`, `task.complete`, `task.delete`, `task.filter`, `task.plan`.          | Natural-language quick capture, safer destructive actions (bulk delete needs confirmation), prompt-injection checks when task text reaches a model, and predictable routing between a local parser and an LLM.              | An intent registry, fixtures, and an eval set. It only pays off once there are at least two execution paths (local parser vs. model vs. tool) or a destructive action to guard. |

### H-MEM: memory, not a task database

H-MEM is a knowledge graph with tiers, hybrid retrieval, provenance, dreaming, and a trust ledger. Its useful role here is **assistant memory**, not task storage:

- Tasks already have a schema and CRUD semantics. Putting them in H-MEM would make simple operations slower and harder to reason about.
- H-MEM earns its keep when the app gains an assistant that must remember **preferences, corrections, and recurring context** across sessions and model swaps.
- Integration shape: retrieve top-N memories before building an AI prompt, then mine the interaction back into memory after the response. The task list remains in `TaskStore`.

### World Model: the part worth borrowing, without the engine

A World Model is an append-only canonical event log with derived views and stable, content-derived IDs. The current app already borrows two of its principles:

1. **Stable IDs.** Tasks use `crypto.randomUUID()` instead of array indices.
2. **Canonical state plus derived views.** `tasks` is canonical; `visibleTasks`, `counts`, and `remainingCount` are recomputed.

The full engine becomes worthwhile only when the product needs **history and convergence**: undo/redo, sync across devices, offline merge, or an audit trail. At that point the change is local to the persistence layer:

```text
TaskEvent[] (append-only)  ->  projector  ->  Task[] (derived)
```

Do not add the operator control plane, enrichment workers, or schema-version migration machinery until there is more than one writer.

### Markovian: only for long model work

Markovian bounds each step to a goal summary, a carryover state, and one chunk. It solves quadratic context growth in long reasoning chains.

This app has no model calls, so there is nothing to bound. It becomes relevant only if a feature asks a model to do **long-horizon work**, for example:

- decompose a large goal into dozens of dependent subtasks,
- run an agent that reviews and rewrites the whole list over many steps,
- generate a multi-day plan with iterative refinement.

A normal "add task" or "suggest a task title" call is a single short request. Wrapping it in Markovian would add latency and complexity with no benefit.

### Scout Intent: the first engine to add if AI arrives

Scout senses intent, guards risk, routes tools, and emits a signed execution contract. It is not a UI state manager; button clicks already have explicit intent and should not be routed through it.

It becomes useful when the app accepts **ambiguous input** or performs **actions chosen by a model**:

- Natural-language capture: "call mom tomorrow at 5 !high" needs intent classification and entity binding.
- A model that can delete or bulk-edit tasks needs a guard and a confirmation contract.
- Multiple execution paths (local regex parser, LLM, external calendar tool) need one router and one audit trail.

The app can get a long way with a tiny local command parser before Scout's full registry, policy packs, and eval harness are justified.

## How they would compose if all four existed

Normal CRUD (add, toggle, edit, delete, filter) stays on the direct path: component -> `TaskStore` -> `localStorage`. No engine belongs in that path.

An AI-assisted flow would look like this:

```text
user input
  -> Scout Intent        classify, guard, route
  -> H-MEM               retrieve preferences and corrections
  -> World Model         read current task/context state
  -> Markovian           only if the job spans many chunks
  -> proposed changes
  -> TaskStore           commit the accepted changes
  -> World Model         append events, rebuild views (if adopted)
  -> H-MEM               mine the outcome back into memory
```

Each engine has a distinct job: Scout decides, H-MEM remembers, World Model grounds, Markovian compresses. None of them should replace `TaskStore` as the place where a user's accepted task changes are committed.

## What not to adopt yet

| Do not adopt                                                                                 | Why not yet                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The full H-MEM engine (tiers, dreaming, sleep cycle, conflict detection, trust ledger)       | There is no model and no memory corpus. A task list is structured data, not mined knowledge.                                |
| The full World Model engine (event sourcing, projections, control plane, enrichment workers) | One user, one writer, `localStorage`, no sync or undo requirement.                                                          |
| Markovian chunking, carryover, checkpoints, and telemetry                                    | No long reasoning jobs. Every user action is a single short operation.                                                      |
| Scout's signed contracts, policy packs, model routing, and eval harness                      | No downstream tools or models to route to. Signing an action the UI already knows how to perform adds ceremony, not safety. |
| Any backend, auth, vector database, or hosted model dependency                               | The brief explicitly asks for a simple local app with no backend.                                                           |

## Recommended adoption order if the product grows

1. **Scout Intent** — once natural-language input or model-chosen actions exist. It is the cheapest engine to justify and the one that prevents unsafe actions.
2. **H-MEM** — once the assistant must remember preferences and corrections across sessions.
3. **World Model** — once history, undo, or multi-device sync becomes a real requirement.
4. **Markovian** — once a single AI job no longer fits comfortably in one context window.

## What each engine does not fix

- H-MEM does not make the list faster, prettier, or easier to use.
- World Model does not add user-facing features by itself; it changes durability and convergence.
- Markovian does not improve short AI responses; it only changes the cost and reach of long ones.
- Scout does not improve unambiguous button clicks; it earns its keep on ambiguous input and risky actions.

## Cheap principles worth keeping now

- Keep `TaskStore` as the only mutation point.
- Keep stable IDs and validate persisted records on load.
- Keep derived state in `computed` signals rather than duplicating it.
- Keep persistence behind the store so `localStorage` can later become IndexedDB or an API without touching components.
- Keep components presentational and `OnPush`.

```
# Meterless Engines in the Angular To-Do App
```

This app implements all four Meterless engines as browser-safe TypeScript ports. The engines are not installed as npm packages; their logic lives in `src/app/engines/` and is wired into the app through services.

The original design review is superseded: the engines are now part of the product, while ordinary CRUD still bypasses them.

## What is implemented

| Engine           | Port location                 | App role                                                                 | Persistence key                |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| **Scout Intent** | `src/app/engines/scout/`      | Classify natural-language input, block injections, gate risky actions    | None; execution contracts only |
| **H-MEM**        | `src/app/engines/hmem/`       | Remember and retrieve user preferences and notes                         | `angular-todo-app.hmem.v1`     |
| **World Model**  | `src/app/engines/world-model/`| Event-sourced task entities, audit trail, merge proposals                | `angular-todo-app.world.v1`    |
| **Markovian**    | `src/app/engines/markovian/`  | Generate bounded plans with per-run chunk configuration and efficiency   | `angular-todo-app.markovian.v1`|

Task records remain in `TaskStore` under `angular-todo-app.tasks`. The engines observe or assist; they do not replace the task store as the commit point.

## Runtime flow

```text
user input
  -> Scout Intent        classify, guard, route
  -> H-MEM               remember or recall preferences
  -> World Model         ground task entities
  -> Markovian           plan long-horizon goals
  -> TaskStore           commit accepted task changes
  -> World Model         append task events
```

Normal UI actions (add, toggle, edit, delete, filter) still go directly from the component to `TaskStore`. The assistant is an additional path, not a wrapper around every click.

## Scout Intent

`ScoutService` loads the app registry from `src/app/engines/scout/app-registry.ts` with the `default` and `adversarial-tight` policy packs.

- Intents cover task add/complete/uncomplete/delete/rename/list/filter/summary/plan, memory remember/recall/forget, and a safe `GENERAL` fallback.
- High-risk actions such as deleting all tasks require explicit confirmation in the assistant panel.
- Prompt-injection patterns are blocked before any action runs.
- Every decision produces a signed execution contract; the app verifies it through `ScoutService.verify`.

The eval adapter is `eval/scout-entry.ts`. It loads the spec fixture registry from `SCOUT_INTENTS_PATH` when provided, otherwise it uses the app registry.

## H-MEM

`MemoryService` wraps a browser-safe `HMEM` instance.

- Explicit "remember" requests are stored as long-term memory with source `user`.
- Recall uses hybrid ranking; if a generic recall query has no strong match, the panel falls back to recent memories.
- Feedback, conflicts, sleep, and dreaming are available in the engine API, but the current UI surfaces memory creation, retrieval, and deletion only.
- Persistence is injected through a localStorage adapter; the engine core has no filesystem dependency.

## World Model

`WorldModelService` owns a `WorldModel` with namespace `todo`.

- Each task is an entity keyed by the stable external key `todo:<task-id>`.
- `TaskStore` syncs add, toggle, and rename operations with `upsertEntitySync`.
- Delete operations append a tombstone and archive the entity.
- The activity panel reads recent events and audit entries; merge proposals are available in the engine API for future review UI.
- Persistence is injected; the browser port does not write `.world/` files.

## Markovian

`PlanningService` wraps a `Markovian` instance with a local deterministic generator.

- "Plan ..." requests run one bounded chunk, so the plan completes without an external model.
- Every run records its own `chunkConfig` snapshot, as required by the spec.
- The assistant shows the plan and the run's efficiency percentage.
- History and cumulative stats persist across reloads.
- The generator can be replaced with a provider-backed `generator` or `stepFn` without changing the engine.

## Conformance and eval

Run the suites from a checkout of the Meterless spec. The exact repository path is environment-specific; the commands below use `<meterless-spec>` as the placeholder.

### Scout eval

```bash
cd <meterless-spec>/engines/scout-intent
npm install
SCOUT_IMPL=<angular-todo-app>/eval/scout-entry.ts \
  npx tsx evals/runner/index.ts all
```

| `intent_top3_recall` | 1.00   |
| `injection_precision`| 1.00   |
| `injection_recall`   | 1.00   |
| `tool_precision`     | 1.00   |
| `clarification_rate` | 0.0625 |
| `override_frequency` | 0.00   |

### H-MEM conformance

```bash
HMEM_IMPL=<angular-todo-app>/src/app/engines/hmem/index.ts \
  npx tsx <meterless-spec>/engines/hmem/conformance/runner.ts
```

Latest result: **13/13 checks passed**.

### World Model conformance

```bash

  npx tsx <meterless-spec>/engines/world-model/conformance/runner.ts
```

Latest result: **8/8 checks passed**.

### Markovian conformance

```bash
  npx tsx <meterless-spec>/engines/markovian/conformance/runner.ts
```

Latest result: **8/8 checks passed**.

## Browser adaptations

The reference implementations are Node-oriented. The ports differ in three deliberate ways:

1. **No filesystem access.** `node:fs` and `node:path` imports are removed. H-MEM, World Model, and Markovian history accept injected `load`/`save` persistence adapters. The app supplies localStorage adapters.
2. **Browser-safe crypto.** Scout uses the dependency-free SHA-256/HMAC implementation in `src/app/engines/shared/crypto.ts` instead of Node crypto.
3. **Synchronous write seams for the UI.** World Model exposes `upsertEntitySync` and `tombstoneSync` so `TaskStore` can project a local mutation immediately. The queued async methods remain available for ingest-style callers.

Internal engine imports are extensionless so the Angular compiler can bundle them. The Node-only Scout adapter imports the engine with an explicit `.ts` extension because it runs under `tsx`.

## Deliberate limits

- The assistant is deterministic and local. There is no remote model, API key, or network dependency.
- Scout's registry covers the app's actual action surface. Adding a new tool means adding an intent, capabilities, examples, and a fixture.
- H-MEM dreaming, sleep consolidation, and conflict auto-resolution are implemented but not exposed in the UI.
- World Model merge proposals are recorded; there is no operator review screen yet.
- Markovian plans are generated locally; long-horizon model-backed planning would replace the generator, not the engine.
- `localStorage` is the only persistence tier. IndexedDB or a backend can replace the adapters without changing engine cores.

## Design rules kept

- `TaskStore` remains the only task mutation point.
- Stable IDs and persisted-record validation are preserved.
- Derived state stays in `computed` signals.
- Components remain presentational and `OnPush`.
- Engines stay framework-free; Angular integration lives in services and components.

1: // H-MEM conformance runner. Executes ANY implementation against the spec's
2: // load-bearing behaviors and prints a scorecard.
3: //
4: //   npx tsx runner.ts                              # runs the reference
5: //   HMEM_IMPL=/abs/path/to/index.ts npx tsx runner.ts   # runs YOURS
6: //
7: // The implementation module must export an HMEM class compatible with
8: // AGENTS.md: constructor({ clock }), add(), query(), feedback(), and the
9: // service surface (store, ledger, sleep, dreaming, conflicts). Assertions here
10: // are the exact tier: formula arithmetic, deltas, gates, and boundaries the
11: // spec fully determines. Absolute score values depend on the embedder and are
12: // NOT asserted, except order where the spec makes order embedding-independent.
13: 
14: import fs from "node:fs";
15: import path from "node:path";
16: import { pathToFileURL, fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
17: 
18: const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
19: const implPath = process.env.HMEM_IMPL ?? path.join(here, "..", "reference", "src", "index.ts");
20: 
21: interface CaseResult {
22:   id: string;
23:   section: string;
24:   description: string;
25:   status: "PASS" | "FAIL";
26:   detail?: string;
27: }
28: 
29: async function loadImpl(): Promise<{ HMEM: new (opts: { clock: () => number }) => any }> {
30:   let mod: Record<string, unknown>;
31:   try {
32:     mod = await import(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(implPath)).href);
33:   } catch (err) {
34:     console.error(`conformance: could not load implementation at ${implPath}`);
35:     console.error(`  ${(err as Error).message}`);
36:     console.error(`  Set HMEM_IMPL to an absolute path exporting an HMEM class.`);
37:     process.exit(2);
38:   }
39:   if (typeof mod.HMEM !== "function") {
40:     console.error(`conformance: module at ${implPath} does not export an HMEM class.`);
41:     console.error(`  Exports found: ${Object.keys(mod).join(", ") || "(none)"}`);
42:     process.exit(2);
43:   }
44:   return mod as never;
45: }
46: 
47: function approx(a: number, b: number, eps = 1e-9): boolean {
48:   return Math.abs(a - b) < eps;
49: }
50: 
51: async function main(): Promise<void> {
52:   const { HMEM } = await loadImpl();
53:   const vectors = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(here, "vectors", "vectors.json"), "utf-8"));
54:   const T0: number = vectors.clock;
55:   const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
56:   const results: CaseResult[] = [];
57:   const ids = new Set<string>();
58: 
59:   const record = (section: string, id: string, description: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) => {
60:     if (ids.has(id)) throw new Error(`duplicate case id ${id}`);
61:     ids.add(id);
62:     return Promise.resolve()
63:       .then(fn)
64:       .then(() => results.push({ id, section, description, status: "PASS" }))
65:       .catch((err: Error) => results.push({ id, section, description, status: "FAIL", detail: err.message }));
66:   };
67:   const assert = (cond: boolean, msg: string) => {
68:     if (!cond) throw new Error(msg);
69:   };
70: 
71:   for (const c of vectors.sections["record-validation"]) {
72:     await record("record-validation", c.id, c.description, () => {
73:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => T0 });
74:       let rejected = false;
75:       try {
76:         hmem.add({ content: c.input.content, source: c.input.source });
77:       } catch {
78:         rejected = true;
79:       }
80:       assert(rejected === (c.expect === "reject"), `expected ${c.expect}, got ${rejected ? "reject" : "accept"}`);
81:     });
82:   }
83: 
84:   for (const c of vectors.sections["feedback-deltas"]) {
85:     await record("feedback-deltas", c.id, c.description, () => {
86:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => T0 });
87:       const m = hmem.add({ content: "feedback target record", confidence: c.start, source: "conformance" });
88:       const accessBefore = m.accessCount;
89:       hmem.feedback(m.id, c.kind);
90:       const after = hmem.store.get(m.id);
91:       assert(approx(after.confidence, c.expectConfidence), `confidence ${after.confidence}, expected ${c.expectConfidence}`);
92:       if (c.expectAccessDelta !== undefined) {
93:         assert(after.accessCount - accessBefore === c.expectAccessDelta, `accessCount delta ${after.accessCount - accessBefore}, expected ${c.expectAccessDelta}`);
94:       }
95:       if (c.expectTag) assert(after.tags.includes(c.expectTag), `missing tag ${c.expectTag}`);
96:     });
97:   }
98: 
99:   for (const c of vectors.sections["ranking-order"]) {
100:     await record("ranking-order", c.id, c.description, () => {
101:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => T0 });
102:       const byKey: Record<string, any> = {};
103:       for (const r of c.records) {
104:         byKey[r.key] = hmem.add({ content: r.content, confidence: r.confidence, layer: r.layer, source: "conformance" });
105:       }
106:       for (const r of c.records) {
107:         if (r.supersededByKey) byKey[r.key].supersededBy = byKey[r.supersededByKey].id;
108:       }
109:       const result = hmem.query(c.query, { threshold: 0, topN: 10 });
110:       const order = result.memories.map((m: any) => m.memory.id);
111:       const expected = c.expectOrder.map((k: string) => byKey[k].id);
112:       for (let i = 0; i < expected.length - 1; i++) {
113:         assert(order.indexOf(expected[i]) < order.indexOf(expected[i + 1]), `expected ${c.expectOrder[i]} before ${c.expectOrder[i + 1]}, got [${order.join(", ")}]`);
114:       }
115:     });
116:   }
117: 
118:   for (const c of vectors.sections["sleep-guardrails"]) {
119:     await record("sleep-guardrails", c.id, c.description, () => {
120:       let now = T0;
121:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => now });
122:       const byKey: Record<string, any> = {};
123:       for (const r of c.records) {
124:         byKey[r.key] = hmem.add({ content: r.content, source: r.source, derivedFrom: r.derivedFrom });
125:       }
126:       now = T0 + c.ageDays * DAY;
127:       const before = JSON.stringify(hmem.store.all().map((m: any) => m.id).sort());
128:       const preview = hmem.sleep.preview();
129:       assert(JSON.stringify(hmem.store.all().map((m: any) => m.id).sort()) === before, "preview mutated the store");
130:       for (const k of c.expectArchived) assert(preview.toArchive.includes(byKey[k].id), `${k} should be archivable`);
131:       for (const k of c.expectProtected) assert(!preview.toArchive.includes(byKey[k].id), `${k} is guardrail-protected and must not archive`);
132:       const report = hmem.sleep.execute(preview);
133:       for (const k of c.expectProtected) assert(hmem.store.get(byKey[k].id) !== undefined, `${k} was deleted despite guardrails`);
134:       assert(typeof report.backupId === "string" && report.backupId.length > 0, "execute must return a backupId");
135:     });
136:   }
137: 
138:   for (const c of vectors.sections["conflict-gate"]) {
139:     await record("conflict-gate", c.id, c.description, () => {
140:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => T0 });
141:       const a = hmem.add({ content: c.a.content, confidence: c.a.confidence, source: "conformance" });
142:       const b = hmem.add({ content: c.b.content, confidence: c.b.confidence, source: "conformance" });
143:       const found = hmem.conflicts.scan();
144:       assert(found.length > 0, "opposing always/never pair on similar content must be detected");
145:       const outcome = hmem.conflicts.autoResolve(found[0]);
146:       assert(outcome === "resolved" || outcome === "queued", `outcome must be resolved or queued, got ${outcome}`);
147:       if (outcome === "resolved") {
148:         const loser = [hmem.store.get(a.id), hmem.store.get(b.id)].find((m: any) => m?.supersededBy);
149:         assert(loser !== undefined, "resolved conflicts must mark the loser supersededBy");
150:       }
151:       assert(hmem.store.get(a.id) && hmem.store.get(b.id), "conflict resolution must never delete records");
152:     });
153:   }
154: 
155:   for (const c of vectors.sections["ledger-audit"]) {
156:     await record("ledger-audit", c.id, c.description, () => {
157:       const hmem = new HMEM({ clock: () => T0 });
158:       const m = hmem.add({ content: "audited record", confidence: c.start, source: "conformance" });
159:       hmem.feedback(m.id, c.kind);
160:       const history = hmem.ledger.history(m.id);
161:       const actions = history.map((h: any) => h.action);

163:       const fb = history[history.length - 1];

165:       assert(approx(fb.newState?.confidence, c.expectNew), `newState.confidence ${fb.newState?.confidence}, expected ${c.expectNew}`);
166:     });
167:   }

172:       for (const r of c.records) hmem.add({ content: r.content, type: r.type, source: "conformance" });
